# scaffold a fuzz harness

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/README.md

  <h1>Anchor</h1>

  <p>
    <strong>Solana Program Framework</strong>

  <p>
    <a href="https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/actions"><img alt="Build Status" src="https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/actions/workflows/tests.yaml/badge.svg" /></a>

[Anchor](https://www.anchor-lang.com/) is a framework providing several convenient developer tools for writing Solana programs (sometimes called 'smart contracts').

- Rust eDSL for writing Solana programs
- [IDL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interface_description_language) specification
- TypeScript package for generating clients from IDL
- CLI and workspace management for developing complete applications

Anchor is the most popular framework for Solana programs.

> [!NOTE]
> If you're familiar with developing in Ethereum's [Solidity](https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/), [Truffle](https://www.trufflesuite.com/), [web3.js](https://github.com/ethereum/web3.js), then using Anchor will be familiar. Although the DSL syntax and semantics are targeted at Solana, the high level flow of writing RPC request handlers, emitting an IDL, and generating clients from IDL is the same.

## Getting Started

For a quickstart guide and in depth tutorials, see the [Anchor book](https://book.anchor-lang.com) and the [Anchor documentation](https://anchor-lang.com).

To jump straight to examples, go [here](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/tree/master/examples). For the latest Rust and TypeScript API documentation, see [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang) and the [typedoc](https://www.anchor-lang.com/docs/clients/typescript).

## Installation

The recommended way to install the Anchor CLI is with the Anchor Version Manager (AVM).

```sh
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/otter-sec/anchor/master/avm/install | sh
```

The installer downloads the latest nightly AVM and Anchor CLI binaries, enables
the nightly channel, and links the `avm` and `anchor` commands into
`~/.cargo/bin` when possible. After that, `anchor` will use the latest cached
nightly build and periodically check for updates.

If you already have AVM installed, you can enable the nightly channel directly:

```sh
avm nightly
```

To leave nightly mode and return to normal AVM version resolution, run:

```sh
avm nightly --disable
```

## Examples

Here's a counter program, where only the designated `authority`
can increment the count.

```rust
use anchor_lang::prelude::*;

declare_id!("Fg6PaFpoGXkYsidMpWTK6W2BeZ7FEfcYkg476zPFsLnS");

#[program]
mod counter {
    use super::*;

    pub fn initialize(ctx: Context<Initialize>, start: u64) -> Result<()> {
        let counter = &mut ctx.accounts.counter;
        counter.authority = *ctx.accounts.authority.key;
        counter.count = start;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn increment(ctx: Context<Increment>) -> Result<()> {
        let counter = &mut ctx.accounts.counter;
        counter.count += 1;
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    #[account(init, payer = authority, space = 48)]
    pub counter: Account<'info, Counter>,
    pub authority: Signer<'info>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Increment<'info> {
    #[account(mut, has_one = authority)]
    pub counter: Account<'info, Counter>,
    pub authority: Signer<'info>,
}

#[account]
pub struct Counter {
    pub authority: Pubkey,
    pub count: u64,
}
```

For more, see the [examples](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/tree/master/examples)
and [tests](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/tree/master/tests) directories.

## Fuzzing

`anchor fuzz` integrates [Crucible](https://github.com/asymmetric-research/crucible) for coverage-guided program fuzzing. See the [fuzzing docs](https://anchor-lang.com/docs/testing/fuzzing) or the [Crucible docs](https://github.com/asymmetric-research/crucible#quick-start).

```sh
# scaffold a fuzz harness
anchor fuzz init program_name

# run a fuzz test
anchor fuzz run program_name test_name --release
```

# Contributing to Anchor

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to Anchor

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Anchor! All contributions are welcome no
matter how big or small. This includes (but is not limited to) filing issues,
adding documentation, fixing bugs, creating examples, and implementing features.

## Finding issues to work on

If you're looking to get started,
check out [good first issues](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22)
or issues where [help is wanted](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22help+wanted%22).
PRs that only correct typos or make minor wording adjustments will be rejected. Fixing typos alongside other non-trivial engineering work is welcome.

If you're considering larger changes or self motivated features, please file an issue
and engage with the maintainers in [Discord](https://discord.gg/NHHGSXAnXk).

## Choosing an issue

If you'd like to contribute, please claim an issue by commenting, forking, and
opening a pull request, even if empty. This allows the maintainers to track who
is working on what issue as to not overlap work.

## Branch Targeting

Pull requests should usually target `master`.

If your change is breaking, open the pull request against `anchor-next`
instead of `master`.

## Issue Guidelines

Please follow these guidelines:

Before coding:

- choose a branch name that describes the issue you're working on
- enable [commit signing](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/signing-commits)

While coding:

- Submit a draft PR asap
- Only change code directly relevant to your PR. Sometimes you might find some code that could really need some refactoring. However, if it's not relevant to your PR, do not touch it. File an issue instead. This allows the reviewer to focus on a single problem at a time.
- If you write comments, do not exceed 80 chars per line. This allows contributors who work with multiple open windows to still read the comments without horizontally scrolling.
- Write adversarial tests. For example, if you're adding a new account type, do not only write tests where the instruction succeeds. Also write tests that test whether the instruction fails, if a check inside the new type is violated.

After coding:

- If you've moved code around, build the docs with `cargo doc --open` and adjust broken links
- Adjust the cli templates if necessary
- If you've added a new folder to the `tests` directory, add it to the [CI](./.github/workflows/tests.yaml).
- Before opening a PR, build, test, and run formatting and lints locally; see the sections below for commands.

## Building and Testing Locally

Use the commands below to validate changes before opening a PR.

### Build

```sh
# Rust workspace
cargo build

# TypeScript packages (run in the package/workspace you changed)
yarn build
```

### Test Categories

#### 1) Rust unit tests

```sh
cargo test
```

#### 2) TypeScript unit tests

```sh
yarn test
```

Run `yarn test` in the relevant package/workspace (for example
`ts/packages/anchor`).

#### 3) Anchor integration tests

```sh
anchor test
```

These are the integration tests under the root `tests/` folder.
Contributors should run the tests that cover their changes and/or add new
test cases.

Integration and other non-Rust tests depend on local TS package linking.
You can set this up in either of these ways:

- Recommended: run `./setup-tests.sh`
- Manual: use `yarn link` to link local Anchor TS packages

For `anchor test`, ensure the `anchor` command points to your local CLI
build (for example via `./setup-tests.sh`, `cargo install --path cli`, or
running the binary from `target` directly).

### AVM and local CLI installs

`cargo install --path cli` writes `anchor` into `~/.cargo/bin/anchor`.
AVM also manages `anchor` in that same location via symlink, so installing
from Cargo overrides AVM version selection until reverted.

To restore AVM-managed behavior:

- uninstall/remove the Cargo-installed binary (`cargo uninstall anchor-cli`
  or `rm ~/.cargo/bin/anchor`)
- re-run AVM so it rewrites the symlink

## Formatting and Linting

If you have edited any Rust or TypeScript/JavaScript code, ensure it is correctly formatted and compatible with our lint suite; this will ensure CI passes and help us quickly review your contribution.

### Rust

In the root workspace, run:

```sh
# Ensure you have the latest nightly version with `rustup update nightly`
cargo +nightly fmt
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

### TypeScript/JavaScript

Enter the relevant JS package (e.g. `tests/`, or `ts/packages/anchor`) and run:

```sh
yarn install --frozen-lockfile
yarn lint:fix
```

# 0-29-0.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/updates/release-notes/0-29-0.mdx

title: 0.29.0
description: Anchor release notes for 0.29.0.

Anchor keeps a [`CHANGELOG.md{:file}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md), but parsing what changed, why it matters, and how to migrate isn't always obvious from the entries. The release notes provide an actionable, digestible view of each release.

## How to update

1. Update `avm`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>cargo</blue> install <dim>--git</dim> https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor <dim>--tag</dim> v0.29.0 avm <dim>--locked</dim>
   ```

2. Update `anchor-cli`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>avm</blue> install latest
   ```

3. Update Anchor crate(s) to `0.29.0`. Optionally run `$ <blue>cargo</blue> update` to refresh other dependencies to the latest compatible versions.

4. Update TS package(s) to `0.29.0`.

## Solana `1.14` is no longer supported

The minimum supported Solana version is now `1.16.0`. All clusters, including mainnet-beta, are running `^1.16`, and a [compatibility issue](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/31960) between `1.14` and `1.16` makes staying on the older version impractical. If you are still on `1.14`, upgrade with:

```console
$ <blue>solana-install</blue> init 1.17.0
```

## Override toolchain for the workspace

`Anchor.toml{:file}` has a new section called `[toolchain]` that allows overriding the current toolchain versions inside the workspace:

```toml
[toolchain]
anchor_version = "0.29.0" # `anchor-cli` version to use
solana_version = "1.17.0" # Solana version to use
```

Both fields are optional. `anchor_version` requires [`avm`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/tree/master/avm) to be installed. Before this release, the `anchor_version` and `solana_version` keys in `Anchor.toml{:file}` only affected Docker verifiable builds. Every command now honors the `[toolchain]` section.

## Install CLI from commit with `avm`

Installing the CLI from a specific commit was historically possible directly through cargo:

```console
$ <blue>cargo</blue> install <dim>--git</dim> https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor <dim>--rev</dim> 6cf200493a307c01487c7b492b4893e0d6f6cb23 anchor-cli <dim>--locked</dim>
```

That approach overrides the `anchor` binary outside of `avm`'s control. As of this release, `avm` natively supports installing and switching between commits.

Pass a `<dim><version></dim>`-`<dim><commit></dim>` pair, a full commit hash, or a short prefix to `$ <blue>avm</blue> install`:

```console
$ <blue>avm</blue> install 0.28.0-6cf200493a307c01487c7b492b4893e0d6f6cb23
$ <blue>avm</blue> install 6cf200493a307c01487c7b492b4893e0d6f6cb23
$ <blue>avm</blue> install 6cf200
```

Activate it with `$ <blue>avm</blue> use`:

```console
$ <blue>avm</blue> use 0.28.0-6cf200493a307c01487c7b492b4893e0d6f6cb23
```

The same identifier also works as the `toolchain.anchor_version` value in `Anchor.toml{:file}`:

```toml
[toolchain]
anchor_version = "0.28.0-6cf200493a307c01487c7b492b4893e0d6f6cb23"
```

## Multiple files template

Programs scaffolded by `$ <blue>anchor</blue> init` and `$ <blue>anchor</blue> new` previously shipped as a single `lib.rs{:file}`. A new template emits the common multi-file layout:

<FileTree>
  <File name="constants.rs" />
  <File name="error.rs" />
  <Dir name="instructions">
    <File name="initialize.rs" />
    <File name="mod.rs" />
  </Dir>
  <File name="lib.rs" />
  <Dir name="state">
    <File name="mod.rs" />
  </Dir>
</FileTree>

Initialize a workspace with this layout:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim><NAME></dim> <dim>--template</dim> multiple
```

Or add a new program with the same layout to an existing workspace:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> new <dim><NAME></dim> <dim>--template</dim> multiple
```

## Upgradeable programs in tests

Upgradeability for programs run under `$ <blue>anchor</blue> test` is now configurable in `Anchor.toml{:file}`. The workspace-wide flag covers every test program:

```toml
[test]
upgradeable = true
```

A `[[test.genesis]]` entry overrides the flag for an individual program:

```toml
[[test.genesis]]
address = "22Y43yTVxuUkoRKdm9thyRhQ3SdgQS7c7kB6UNCiaczD"
program = "swap.so"
upgradeable = true
```

## Lamport utilities

Transferring lamports from a PDA used to require awkward type juggling. The new `sub_lamports(){:rs}` and `add_lamports(){:rs}` helpers replace the borrow dance:

```rust showLineNumbers=false del={1-2} add={3-4}
**ctx.accounts.from.to_account_info().try_borrow_mut_lamports()? -= amount;
**ctx.accounts.to.to_account_info().try_borrow_mut_lamports()? += amount;
ctx.accounts.from.sub_lamports(amount)?;
ctx.accounts.to.add_lamports(amount)?;
```

`get_lamports(){:rs}` similarly replaces the read-side dance:

```rust showLineNumbers=false del={1} add={2}
let lamports = ctx.accounts.my_account.to_account_info().lamports();
let lamports = ctx.accounts.my_account.get_lamports();
```

These helpers are also more efficient than the manual form. `to_account_info(){:rs}` clones the underlying data internally, while the new methods take a reference to it.

## Type-safe context bumps

Before this release, `ctx.bumps{:rs}` was a `BTreeMap<String, u8>{:rs}`, which gave no type safety for the account-name keys:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
let bump = *ctx.bumps.get("my_account").unwrap();
```

It is now an auto-generated struct that holds each bump as a named field, enabling completion and rejecting typos at compile time:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
let bump = ctx.bumps.my_account;
```

The struct form is also faster than `BTreeMap{:rs}`, which is heap-allocated and occasionally has to resize.

## `idl-build` feature

IDLs can now be generated via compilation rather than parsing. Enable it by adding the `idl-build` feature to the program's `Cargo.toml{:file}`:

```toml
[features]
idl-build = ["anchor-lang/idl-build"]
```

The IDL will be built automatically when you run `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` but if you'd like to only generate the IDL, run `$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl build`.

Every crate involved in IDL generation must be added to the `idl-build` feature list:

```toml
[features]
idl-build = [
    "anchor-lang/idl-build",
    "anchor-spl/idl-build",
    "another-program/idl-build"
]
```

Compile-time checks are supported, as are external types from other Anchor programs (provided the external crate also exposes an `idl-build` feature, like `another-program/idl-build` above). Two crates can use the same type name (for example `some_module::MyType{:rs}` and `another_module::MyType{:rs}`) without collision. Generation is noticeably slower than the default parsing-based method due to Rust compile times. Most of the pipeline works well, but rough edges remain. If you run into one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues).

## Type aliases

Anchor IDL now supports type aliases:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
pub type U8Array = [u8; 8];

#[program]
pub mod my_program {
    use super::*;

    pub fn type_alias(ctx: Context<TypeAlias>, u8_array: U8Array) -> Result<()> {
        msg!("{:?}", u8_array);
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct TypeAlias {}
```

Generates the following IDL:

```json
{
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "name": "my_program",
  "instructions": [
    {
      "name": "typeAlias",
      "accounts": [],
      "args": [
        {
          "name": "u8Array",
          "type": {
            "defined": "U8Array"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "types": [
    {
      "name": "U8Array",
      "type": {
        "kind": "alias",
        "value": {
          "array": ["u8", 8]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

This example currently works only with the default parsing-based IDL generator. Type aliases over built-in Rust types are not yet handled correctly by `idl-build` ([#2640](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues/2640)).

## Export `mpl-token-metadata`

`anchor-spl` with the `metadata` feature now re-exports the `mpl-token-metadata` crate. Drop the direct dependency to avoid version conflicts:

```toml title="Cargo.toml" del={3}
[dependencies]
anchor-spl = { version = "0.29.0", features = ["metadata"] }
mpl-token-metadata = "1.13.1"
```

The crate is reachable through `anchor_spl::metadata{:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
use anchor_spl::metadata::mpl_token_metadata;
```

## TypeScript SDK improvements

`Program.addEventListener{:ts}` is now strongly typed. Event names and the event passed to the callback both carry their proper types instead of `any{:ts}`.

`anchor.workspace{:ts}` lazy-loads programs on demand, so programs that aren't used in the test suite no longer get loaded or trigger errors.

JavaScript convention uses camelCase for property names, but programs were previously accessed via PascalCase (e.g. `anchor.workspace.MyProgram{:ts}`), which is unintuitive. Both variations now work:

```ts showLineNumbers=false
const camel = anchor.workspace.myProgram
const pascal = anchor.workspace.MyProgram
```

The `assert` and `base64-js` dependencies have been removed.

## New Docker image

The previous image, [`projectserum/build`](https://hub.docker.com/r/projectserum/build), has been deprecated. The new image is [`backpackapp/build`](https://hub.docker.com/r/backpackapp/build), which you can pull with `$ <blue>docker</blue> pull backpackapp/build:v0.29.0`. `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--verifiable</dim>` works against the new image.

## Enhanced performance

`0.29.0` improves performance across the board, most notably reducing [binary size](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/master/bench/BINARY_SIZE.md#0290) by roughly 36% relative to `0.28.0`. Similar wins are tracked for [compute units](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/master/bench/COMPUTE_UNITS.md#0290) and [stack memory](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/master/bench/STACK_MEMORY.md#0290). Exact numbers vary between programs, but the overall direction is consistent.

See the full list of changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#0290---2023-10-16).

---

# 0-30-0.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/updates/release-notes/0-30-0.mdx

title: 0.30.0
description: Anchor release notes for 0.30.0.

These notes cover the main changes in `0.30.0`. The complete list of notable changes lives in the [`CHANGELOG.md{:file}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.30.0/CHANGELOG.md#0300---2024-04-15).

## How to upgrade

1. Update `avm`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>cargo</blue> install <dim>--git</dim> https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor <dim>--tag</dim> v0.30.0 avm <dim>--locked</dim>
   ```

2. Update `anchor-cli`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>avm</blue> install latest
   ```

3. Update Anchor crate(s) to `0.30.0`. Optionally, run `$ <blue>cargo</blue> update` to update other dependencies to the latest compatible versions.

4. Update TS package(s) to `0.30.0`.

## Recommended Solana version

This release supports any Solana version above `1.16`, with `1.18.8` recommended. Upgrade Solana tools with:

```console
$ <blue>solana-install</blue> init 1.18.8
```

## IDL

The IDL type specification and generation have been rewritten. See [PR #2824](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/2824) for the design discussion.

### `idl-build` feature

`idl-build` feature is now required in your program's `Cargo.toml{:file}` definition in order for the IDL generation to work.

Without this feature, `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` outputs:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build
Error: `idl-build` feature is missing. To solve, add

[features]
idl-build = ["anchor-lang/idl-build"]

in `<PATH_TO_CARGO_TOML>`.
```

Every crate used to generate type definitions for the IDL must be listed in the `idl-build` feature, for example `anchor-spl/idl-build` or `some-program/idl-build`.

## Lang

### Dependency free program declaration

Depending on multiple crates that pull in different Anchor versions has long been painful. The new `declare_program!(){:rs}` macro generates a program client directly from an IDL, removing the runtime version coupling:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
declare_program!(program_name);
```

`program_name` matches a file in the workspace's `idls{:dir}` directory, so the example above expects `idls/program_name.json{:file}` to exist. The generated client supports both on-chain CPI and off-chain RPC usage, sidestepping [dependency hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependency_hell). See the [on-chain CPI example](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.30.0/tests/declare-program/programs/declare-program/src/lib.rs) and the [macro documentation](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang/0.30.0/anchor_lang/macro.declare_program.html) for full details.

### Token extensions

#### Constraints

New account constraints cover the [Token Extensions (Token 2022)](https://solana.com/solutions/token-extensions) program. Each field is referenced under the `extensions` prefix and joined with `::`, for example `extensions::group_pointer::authority = <EXPR>{:rs}`.

| Extension              | Fields                          |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `group_pointer`        | `authority`, `group_address`    |
| `group_member_pointer` | `authority`, `member_address`   |
| `metadata_pointer`     | `authority`, `metadata_address` |
| `close_authority`      | `authority`                     |
| `permanent_delegate`   | `delegate`                      |
| `transfer_hook`        | `authority`, `program_id`       |

Each constraint works with or without the `init` constraint. The [token-extensions integration test](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.30.0/tests/spl/token-extensions/programs/token-extensions/src/instructions.rs) shows the full set in use.

#### CPI wrappers

`anchor-spl` now ships CPI wrappers for the Token Extensions program under `anchor_spl::token_2022_extensions{:rs}`.

### `#[interface]` attribute

Transfer hooks can now be wired up with the new `#[interface]{:rs}` attribute, which replaces Anchor's default instruction discriminator with the interface instruction's discriminator. Two values are currently supported: `spl_transfer_hook_interface::initialize_extra_account_meta_list{:rs}` and `spl_transfer_hook_interface::execute{:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
mod my_hook_program {
    #[interface(spl_transfer_hook_interface::initialize_extra_account_meta_list)]
    pub fn initialize(ctx: Context<Initialize>, metas: Vec<AnchorExtraAccountMeta>) -> Result<()> {
        /* ... */
    }

    #[interface(spl_transfer_hook_interface::execute)]
    pub fn execute(ctx: Context<Execute>, amount: u64) -> Result<()> {
        /* ... */
    }
}
```

### Optional bumps

Bumps for unspecified optional accounts no longer default to `u8::MAX{:rs}`. The optional bump type is now `Option<u8>{:rs}`, and missing entries are `None{:rs}`.

### Less heap allocations

Borsh's [`try_to_vec`](https://github.com/near/borsh-rs/blob/79097e3c71ae469a101b4828457792bcf8be7f5f/borsh/src/ser/mod.rs#L47-L51), which Anchor uses for events, CPI, and return data, allocates [1024 bytes](https://github.com/near/borsh-rs/blob/79097e3c71ae469a101b4828457792bcf8be7f5f/borsh/src/ser/mod.rs#L19) per call regardless of payload size. The default has been lowered to 256 bytes. The new `InstructionData::write_to(){:rs}` method also writes into an existing allocation, avoiding the fresh allocation `InstructionData::data(){:rs}` creates.

## CLI

### Priority fees in CLI

Landing transactions on mainnet-beta increasingly requires priority fees. IDL commands now accept a `<dim>--priority-fee</dim>` argument:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl erase-authority <dim>--program-id</dim> <dim><PROGRAM_ID></dim> <dim>--priority-fee</dim> 9000
```

Without an explicit value, the median fee of the last 150 confirmed slots is used.

### `<dim>--no-idl</dim>` flag on builds

IDL generation requires a full program build. When the program's public API hasn't changed, the `<dim>--no-idl</dim>` flag skips IDL regeneration:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--no-idl</dim>
```

### IDL buffer is closed after `idl upgrade`

After an IDL upgrade, the buffer account is closed and its lamports returned to the IDL authority.

### Pass deploy arguments to `solana-cli`

Arguments after `--` are forwarded from `$ <blue>anchor</blue> deploy` to `$ <blue>solana</blue> program deploy`:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> deploy <dim>--</dim> <dim>--final</dim>
```

### Verifiable deployments

Like verifiable builds, deployments can now use the verifiable build artifact instead of the default build:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> deploy <dim>--verifiable</dim>
```

### Accept package name as program name

The `<dim>--program-name</dim>` (`<dim>-p</dim>`) argument now accepts a program's package name in addition to its snake_case lib name:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>-p</dim> my-program
```

### Deactivate test-validator features

Test-validator features can now be deactivated from `Anchor.toml{:file}`:

```toml
[test.validator]
deactivate_feature = ["GDH5TVdbTPUpRnXaRyQqiKUa7uZAbZ28Q2N9bhbKoMLm", "zkiTNuzBKxrCLMKehzuQeKZyLtX2yvFcEKMML8nExU8"]
```

### Crate and package compatibility

Mismatched versions of `anchor-cli`, `anchor-lang`, and `@otter-sec/anchor` can lead to unexpected behavior. This release prints a warning when the three don't agree.

### Explicit `overflow-checks` flag

Cargo's [`overflow-checks`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#overflow-checks) is implicitly off by default. Workspaces scaffolded by `$ <blue>anchor</blue> init` enabled it, but Anchor never enforced the setting on existing workspaces. As of this release, `overflow-checks` in the workspace `Cargo.toml{:file}` must be set explicitly to either `true` or `false`.

### Wildcard pattern in `Anchor.toml{:file}`

`workspace.members` and `workspace.exclude` now support a simple trailing wildcard:

```toml
[workspace]
members = ["programs/*"]
```

More complex glob patterns are not yet supported.

### `cargo build-sbf` is now the default

Previously `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` invoked `$ <blue>cargo</blue> build-bpf`. Because `build-bpf` is deprecated, `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` now defaults to `$ <blue>cargo</blue> build-sbf`. The old behavior is still available with:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--arch</dim> bpf
```

### Run multiple commands in scripts

Scripts in `Anchor.toml{:file}` now support multiple commands chained with `&&`:

```toml
[scripts]
test-all = "cargo test && yarn run ts-mocha tests/**/*.ts"
```

Run the script with:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> run test-all
```

### Test only a specified program

A single program in a multi-program workspace can be tested with `<dim>--program-name</dim>` (`<dim>-p</dim>`):

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> test <dim>--program-name</dim> example
```

### Rust test template

Initialize a workspace with a Rust test template instead of the default TypeScript:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim>--test-template</dim> rust
```

## TypeScript

### Account resolution

Account resolution lets clients fill in accounts automatically rather than passing every one explicitly. The TS library's resolution logic has been overhauled. Most of those changes are internal, but the user-facing surface around `.accounts(){:ts}` has changed.

Previously, all accounts on the builder were typed as partial, with no way to know which ones the IDL could resolve. The transaction builder now exposes three methods:

- `.accounts(){:ts}` is fully type-safe against the IDL's resolution fields, so only the accounts that can't be resolved need to be passed.
- `.accountsPartial(){:ts}` preserves the old behavior, accepting any account including resolvable ones.
- `.accountsStrict(){:ts}` opts out of resolution entirely and requires every account to be passed manually (unchanged from before).

Existing `.accounts(){:ts}` calls may stop type-checking. Either rename them to `.accountsPartial(){:ts}` to keep the old behavior, or drop the accounts the IDL can resolve:

```ts title="example.ts" showLineNumbers=false del={1-8} add={9}
await program.methods
  .init()
  .accounts({
    pda: ...,
    signer: ...,
    systemProgram: ...,
  })
  .rpc()
await program.methods.init().rpc()
```

### Magic account names

The TS library no longer autofills common program and sysvar accounts based on field names like `systemProgram`. The IDL's new `address` field resolves programs and sysvars directly, removing the need for the name-based magic.

### Case conversion

The TS library's internals were riddled with case-conversion logic before string comparisons, forcing libraries built on Anchor to do the same. The IDL and the TS library now both use consistent camelCase throughout.

### No more program id

The `programId{:ts}` parameter of `Program{:ts}` has been removed. The new IDL stores the program id in its `address` field:

```ts showLineNumbers=false del={1} add={2}
new Program(idl, programId)
new Program(idl)
```

### Optional provider options

The `opts{:ts}` parameter of `AnchorProvider{:ts}` is now optional:

```ts showLineNumbers=false del={1} add={2}
new AnchorProvider(connection, wallet, {})
new AnchorProvider(connection, wallet)
```

### Type changes

Too many type changes to enumerate here, especially around the IDL. See [`idl.ts{:file}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.30.0/ts/packages/anchor/src/idl.ts) for the new types.

See the full list of notable changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.30.0/CHANGELOG.md#0300---2024-04-15).

---

# 0-30-1.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/updates/release-notes/0-30-1.mdx

title: 0.30.1
description: Anchor release notes for 0.30.1.

`0.30.1` is a quality-of-life patch release. There are no major breaking changes from `0.30.0`.

## How to upgrade

1. Update `anchor-cli`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>avm</blue> install 0.30.1
   ```

2. Update Anchor crate(s) to `0.30.1`.

3. Update TS package(s) to `0.30.1`.

## Recommended Solana version

This release supports any Solana version above `1.17.3`, with `1.18.17` recommended. Upgrade Solana tools with:

```console
$ <blue>solana-install</blue> init 1.18.17
```

## IDL

### Convert legacy IDLs

The IDL crate gained support for converting legacy IDLs (pre-Anchor v0.30) to the new spec. Add the `convert` feature to enable it programmatically:

```toml title="Cargo.toml"
anchor-lang-idl = { version = "0.1.1", features = ["convert"] }
```

Then call [`convert_idl`](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang-idl/0.1.1/anchor_lang_idl/convert/fn.convert_idl.html). The same conversion is also exposed as the [`idl convert`](#idl-convert-command) CLI command.

### Unsupported seed expressions

Some seed expressions cannot currently be stored in the IDL. A representative case is the math expression `&(my_account.data + 1).to_le_bytes(){:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct SeedMathExpr<'info> {
    #[account(seeds = [&(my_account.data + 1).to_le_bytes()], bump)]
    pub math_expr_account: UncheckedAccount<'info>,
    pub my_account: Account<'info, MyAccount>,
}

#[account]
pub struct MyAccount {
    data: u64,
}
```

A regression in IDL generation had been surfacing such expressions as compile errors. The compile errors are gone, with the side effect that clients cannot automatically resolve these accounts either.

### Fields with `address{:rs}` constraint

Field expressions used as an address constraint no longer fail IDL generation:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    #[account(address = my_account.authority)]
    pub authority: UncheckedAccount<'info>,
    pub my_account: Account<'info, MyAccount>,
}

#[account]
pub struct MyAccount {
    authority: u64,
}
```

Such accounts still don't resolve automatically when the constraint expression isn't constant. The `has_one{:rs}` constraint is preferable in those cases:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    pub authority: UncheckedAccount<'info>,
    #[account(has_one = authority)]
    pub my_account: Account<'info, MyAccount>,
}
```

### Override `nightly` version on builds

IDL generation uses the `nightly` compiler, which can fail to build on certain nightly versions. The toolchain can now be pinned via the `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` environment variable.

### Recursive generation

Recursive external type resolution during IDL generation no longer produces a compile error. See [PR #2946](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/2946) for the underlying cause.

### New spec crate

Adding features to the IDL crate (such as the [`convert{:rs}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/2986) feature) previously forced a version bump even when the spec itself was unchanged. The IDL spec now lives in its own [crate](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang-idl-spec), whose version is recorded in the `idl.metadata.spec{:rs}` field. The new spec crate is also re-exported through [`anchor_lang_idl::types{:rs}`](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang-idl/0.1.1/anchor_lang_idl/types/index.html) for convenience.

## CLI

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl convert` command

Convert a legacy IDL JSON file to the new spec:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl convert <dim><PATH_TO_IDL_JSON></dim>
```

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl type` command

Generate a TypeScript IDL type (with camelCase fields) from an existing IDL JSON file:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl type <dim><PATH_TO_IDL_JSON></dim>
```

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl build` toolchain override

See [the IDL section](#override-nightly-version-on-builds) for context. The CLI honors the same environment variable:

```console
$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN="nightly-2024-05-09" <blue>anchor</blue> idl build
```

### Automatic program id updates

When building a program for the first time, the program id declarations are updated automatically if `Anchor.toml{:file}` has no `[programs.localnet]{:toml}` entry. This is equivalent to running `$ <blue>anchor</blue> keys sync`, but happens only on that first build.

### Upgradeable program clones

A breaking change in Solana `1.17.12` left programs cloned through `[[test.validator.clone]]` unusable in the test validator. The minimal repro:

```toml
[test.validator]
url = "https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com"

[[test.validator.clone]]
address = "TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb"
```

The fix landed on both the Anchor and Solana sides and requires `solana-cli >= 1.18.10`.

### File system error improvements

Rust's default file-not-found error omits the offending path, which makes debugging painful. Filesystem errors raised by Anchor now include the path.

## Lang

### Using legacy IDLs with `declare_program!{:rs}`

[`declare_program!(){:rs}`](https://www.anchor-lang.com/release-notes/0.30.0#dependency-free-program-declaration) now accepts legacy (pre-v0.30) IDLs. The macro works as long as the legacy spec can describe the program faithfully. Programs that use non-default features (zero-copy, custom `repr{:rs}`, etc.) may produce a declaration that fails to compile or is silently incorrect.

There are two paths around this. The first is to run `$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl convert` and patch the result by hand. The second, preferred path is to upgrade the program to v0.30 and regenerate its IDL, since the new IDL spec was added precisely because the legacy spec couldn't describe modern programs reliably. If dependency upgrades are blocking, strip them. IDL generation only inspects signatures, so program logic and non-Anchor dependencies can be deleted from the temporary build. The [`spl-token` IDL stub](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/cc43e67399ad50cf7d33466f7bcd7e6dcee88ae2/ts/packages/spl-token/program/lib.rs) demonstrates the minimal shape required.

### `declare_program!{:rs}` fixes

Several inputs that should have worked previously caused `declare_program!(){:rs}` to fail compilation:

- Defined types (e.g. `struct{:rs}`s) used as instruction parameters
- Types with `const{:rs}` generics
- `Vec<u8>{:rs}` arguments
- Instructions with a non-unit return type
- Optional accounts in client-generated code
- The `bytemuckunsafe` account serialization mode

Tuple struct fields, which previously inherited Rust's private default, are now generated as public.

### `pubkey!{:rs}` macro

[`solana-program`](https://docs.rs/solana-program/1.18.17/solana_program/index.html) provides [`pubkey!{:rs}`](https://docs.rs/solana-program/1.18.17/solana_program/macro.pubkey.html) for compile-time pubkey literals:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
let key = pubkey!("11111111111111111111111111111111");
```

```rust showLineNumbers=false
use std::str::FromStr;
let key = Pubkey::from_str("11111111111111111111111111111111").unwrap();
```

The macro previously expanded to `::solana_program{:rs}`, so consumers had to include `solana-program` directly even when using Anchor. `pubkey!(){:rs}` is now re-exported from `anchor_lang::prelude{:rs}`, and `solana_program{:rs}` is itself re-exported from `anchor_lang{:rs}`, so the direct `solana-program` dependency can be dropped from `Cargo.toml{:file}` if it was added solely for this macro.

### `ID_CONST{:rs}` constant

[`declare_id!(){:rs}`](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang/0.30.1/anchor_lang/macro.declare_id.html) and [`declare_program!(){:rs}`](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang/0.30.1/anchor_lang/macro.declare_program.html) declare `ID{:rs}` as `static{:rs}`, which prevents compile-time use. Both macros now also emit `ID_CONST{:rs}`, the same value declared as `const{:rs}` so it can participate in const evaluation.

### Stack usage of token extensions

The [token extensions constraints](https://www.anchor-lang.com/release-notes/0.30.0#token-extensions) added in `0.30.0` use less stack.

### Error propagation from integer conversion errors

Integer conversion errors now propagate through `?{:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
let n: i32 = u32::MAX.try_into()?;
```

## SPL

### Export ATA crate

[`spl-associated-token-account`](https://crates.io/crates/spl-associated-token-account) is now re-exported from `anchor_spl::associated_token{:rs}`. Drop the direct dependency the same way [`mpl-token-metadata`](https://www.anchor-lang.com/release-notes/0.29.0#export-mpl-token-metadata) was dropped in `0.29.0`:

```toml title="Cargo.toml" del={3}
[dependencies]
anchor-spl = "0.30.1"
spl-associated-token-account = "3.0.2"
```

## TypeScript

### ATA resolution

[Account resolution](https://www.anchor-lang.com/release-notes/0.30.0#account-resolution) now also covers associated token accounts. Instructions that include ATAs now type-error when those accounts are passed to `.accounts(){:ts}`. Drop them from the call so the resolver can fill them in.

### Defined types in generics

Defined types (structs, enums, or type aliases) used as generic arguments no longer fail IDL generation:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
param: GenericStruct<MyStruct>,
```

### Versioned transactions

`AnchorProvider{:ts}` now sets `maxSupportedTransactionVersion{:ts}` correctly when sending versioned transactions.

### New errors package

Anchor's TS error definitions now live in their own package, [`@coral-xyz/anchor-errors`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@coral-xyz/anchor-errors).

See the full list of notable changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.30.1/CHANGELOG.md#0301---2024-06-20).

---

# 0-31-0.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/updates/release-notes/0-31-0.mdx

title: 0.31.0
description: Anchor release notes for 0.31.0.

`0.31.0` is the last major release before v1. These notes cover the most significant changes (see [`CHANGELOG.md{:file}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.31.0/CHANGELOG.md#0310---2025-03-08) for all changes).

## How to upgrade

1. Install the latest version of `avm`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>cargo</blue> install <dim>--git</dim> https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor avm <dim>--locked</dim> <dim>--force</dim>
   ```

   This is required for the new prebuilt binary install path. See [Install from binary](#install-from-binary).

2. Update `anchor-cli`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>avm</blue> install 0.31.0
   ```

3. Update Anchor crate(s) to `0.31.0`.

4. Update TS package(s) to `0.31.0`.

## Recommended Solana version

The recommended Solana version is `2.1.0`. Several Solana binaries have been renamed under the [Agave transition](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/wiki/Agave-Transition), so this upgrade involves replacing the toolchain entirely. Install the new tooling with:

```console
$ <blue>sh</blue> <dim>-c</dim> "$(curl <dim>-sSfL</dim> https://release.anza.xyz/v2.1.0/install)"
```

Setting `toolchain.solana_version` in `Anchor.toml{:file}` handles this automatically. See [Automatic Agave transition](#automatic-agave-transition).

## AVM

### Install from binary

`$ <blue>avm</blue> install` now downloads prebuilt binaries from GitHub by default. Supported targets:

- `aarch64-apple-darwin`
- `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- `x86_64-apple-darwin`
- `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`

Pass `<dim>--from-source</dim>` to the `install` command to fall back to building from source (required on unsupported platforms).

## CLI

### Automatic Agave transition

As noted in [Recommended Solana version](#recommended-solana-version), several Solana binaries have been renamed to Agave. `solana-install` is deprecated as of `1.18.19` and logs a deprecation banner that older Anchor versions fail to parse:

```text
⚠️  solana-install is deprecated and will be discontinued when v1.18 is no longer supported. Please switch to Agave: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/wiki/Agave-Transition
```

When `solana_version` in `[toolchain]` is greater than `1.18.19`, Anchor now installs and switches to `agave-install` automatically:

```toml
[toolchain]
solana_version = "2.1.0"
```

### `solana-program` warning

Adding `solana-program` as a direct dependency of an Anchor program risks version conflicts between Solana v1 and v2 crates. Builds that include it now print a warning:

```text
WARNING: Adding `solana-program` as a separate dependency might cause conflicts.
To solve, remove the `solana-program` dependency and use the exported crate from `anchor-lang`.
`use solana_program` becomes `use anchor_lang::solana_program`.
Program name: `my-program`
```

### Pass `cargo` args to IDL build

`$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` and `$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl build` now forward `cargo` arguments through to the IDL build command, so passing `--features` through `--` builds the program and its IDL with the feature enabled:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--</dim> <dim>--features</dim> my-feature
```

### `<dim>--no-idl</dim>` flag for tests

When the program changes but its public API doesn't, regenerating the IDL is wasted work. Mirroring [`<dim>--no-idl</dim>` on builds](./0-30-0#--no-idl-flag-on-builds), the test command now accepts the same flag:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> test <dim>--no-idl</dim>
```

### `mollusk` test template

Initialize a workspace with the new [`mollusk`](/docs/v1/testing/mollusk/) test template:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init my-program <dim>--test-template</dim> mollusk
```

### `clean`

`$ <blue>anchor</blue> clean` now also removes the generated `.anchor{:dir}` directory. The command behaves like `$ <blue>cargo</blue> clean`, but preserves program keypairs.

### Automatic IDL conversion

In v0.30, legacy (pre-v0.30) IDLs had to be converted with `$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl convert` before any other command could use them. Most CLI commands now perform that conversion transparently, so legacy and new IDLs work interchangeably. `idl fetch` is the one exception and still emits the on-chain bytes verbatim.

### Package manager

Anchor has historically defaulted to `yarn`, and switching was awkward because several commands hard-required `yarn` on PATH. That coupling is gone. Specify the package manager in `Anchor.toml{:file}`:

```toml
[toolchain]
package_manager = "npm"
```

Or pass it when creating a new workspace:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim><NAME></dim> <dim>--package-manager</dim> npm
```

The supported values are `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm`. The default is `yarn`.

### Shell completions

Shell completions can now be generated for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell. See [Shell completions](/docs/v1/get-started/installation/#shell-completions).

## Lang

### Stack memory improvements

Stack usage from `init` constraints has been reduced significantly, and stack warnings on builds are now reliable when targeting Solana v2 (`platform-tools v1.42`). The rest of this section explains why. Skip to [Custom discriminators](#custom-discriminators) if you don't need the background.

The most common source of stack-violation errors in Anchor programs is the generated `try_accounts(){:rs}` function, where instruction deserialization and constraint validation both run. Co-locating that work is convenient for constraints, but it makes it trivial to overshoot the SVM's fixed 4096-byte stack just by adding accounts. The mangled build log usually looks like:

```text
Error: Function _ZN71_$LT$pr..Test$u20$as$u20$anchor_lang..Accounts$LT$pr..TestBumps$GT$GT$12try_accounts17h5572074d55b9e638E Stack offset of 4112 exceeded max offset of 4096 by 16 bytes, please minimize large stack variables.
```

Three external developments compounded the problem. Rust/LLVM changes in Solana v1.18 increased `try_accounts(){:rs}`'s stack footprint, lowering the threshold for hitting violations. The stack-warning logs were unreliable, so going over the limit didn't always surface at build time. And the ["Account data direct mapping"](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29708) feature, which is on by default in the local validator, meant that exceeding the stack at runtime triggered [undefined behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undefined_behavior) rather than a clean panic.

Undefined behavior is particularly hard to debug because tests can appear to pass while a different input silently corrupts account bytes. Reported instances include [#2955](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues/2955), [#3113](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues/3113), and [#3196](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues/3196).

The unreliable warnings are fixed in Solana v2's `platform-tools v1.42`, so build-time warnings are now trustworthy. The largest contributor to stack pressure was identified as the `init` constraint, which expanded into a long inline block inside `try_accounts(){:rs}` and stacked badly when multiple `init` accounts were used. The expansion now lives inside an immediately-invoked closure ([#2939](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/2939)), giving each invocation its own stack frame. Looking further out, [SIMD-0166](https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-improvement-documents/pull/166) proposes dynamic stack frames as a runtime-level fix.

Stack-related problems should be considerably rarer on Anchor v0.31 + Solana v2. Lingering issues are tracked in [otter-sec/anchor#3097](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/issues/3097).

### Custom discriminators

Anchor's discriminator handling had several long-standing limitations:

- 8 bytes is sometimes too costly given Solana's 1232-byte transaction size cap
- The `Discriminator{:rs}` trait had a fixed-size `[u8; 8]{:rs}` field, blocking implementations for non-Anchor programs (including `declare_program!(){:rs}`)
- Discriminators were not customizable
- Renaming the underlying type changed its discriminator, breaking deployed programs

This release adds support for custom discriminators. The default 8-byte derivation is unchanged. The `discriminator` argument on Anchor attribute macros opts into an explicit value:

- `#[account(discriminator = 1)]{:rs}`
- `#[event(discriminator = [1, 2])]{:rs}`
- `#[instruction(discriminator = MY_CONST)]{:rs}`

Any constant expression is accepted on the right-hand side, with the [`custom-discriminator` integration test](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.31.0/tests/custom-discriminator/programs/custom-discriminator/src/lib.rs) exercising the full surface area.

Discriminators must remain unique within a program. Any length is allowed at the trait level (including zero, since some non-Anchor programs like SPL Token have no account discriminator at all), but IDL generation rejects empty discriminators for safety. Programs without discriminators must not rely on the discriminator for safety checks.

IDL generation also rejects ambiguous discriminators, meaning values where one is a prefix of another. With 1-byte discriminators this gets restrictive quickly. An account with discriminator `[1]{:rs}` precludes any other discriminator starting with `1` (such as `[1, 2, 3, 4]{:rs}`), so leave headroom when picking short values.

Custom discriminators also unlock first-class non-Anchor program support via [`declare_program!(){:rs}`](./0-30-0#dependency-free-program-declaration) on the Rust side and the TypeScript client.

### `Discriminator{:rs}` trait

The `discriminator(){:rs}` method of the `Discriminator{:rs}` trait has been removed. Replace any `discriminator(){:rs}` call site with the `DISCRIMINATOR{:rs}` associated constant.

The trait itself is now re-exported from `anchor_lang::prelude{:rs}` so the common pattern of hardcoding the 8-byte discriminator length can be replaced with the trait's associated constant:

```rs showLineNumbers=false del={1} add={2}
space = 8 + ...
space = MyAccount::DISCRIMINATOR.len() + ...
```

### `LazyAccount{:rs}`

`LazyAccount<'info, T>{:rs}` is an experimental drop-in replacement for `Account<'info, T>{:rs}` aimed at performance-sensitive paths. See [its documentation](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang/0.31.0/anchor_lang/accounts/lazy_account/struct.LazyAccount.html) for whether it fits the workload. Using `LazyAccount{:rs}` requires enabling the `lazy-account` feature on `anchor-lang`.

### `cfg{:rs}` attribute on instructions

`cfg{:rs}` attributes are now supported on instructions:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
#[program]
mod my_program {
    #[cfg(feature = "my-feature")]
    pub fn my_feature(ctx: Context<MyFeature>) -> Result<()> {}
}
```

### Unnamed and unit structs with `InitSpace{:rs}`

Unnamed and unit structs gained Anchor support in v0.30, but `#[derive(InitSpace)]{:rs}` didn't work for them. Both shapes are now supported:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(InitSpace)]
pub struct Unnamed(pub u64, #[max_len(64)] pub Vec<u8>);

#[derive(InitSpace)]
pub struct Unit;
```

### Account parser

`declare_program!(){:rs}` now also generates an account parser:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
declare_program!(my_program);
```

This will generate something similar to:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
pub enum Account {
    SomeAccount(SomeAccount),
    OtherAccount(OtherAccount),
}
```

Call `my_program::utils::Account::try_from_bytes(){:rs}` to deserialize any account owned by the program into the right variant.

### `declare_program!{:rs}` improvements

The following issues related to [`declare_program!{:rs}`](/docs/v1/clients/declare-program/) have been fixed:

- Being unable to use constant bytes ([#3287](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3287))
- Missing docs from the generated constants ([#3311](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3311))
- Compilation errors related to incorrectly adding `derive{:rs}`s and `repr{:rs}`s to type aliases ([#3504](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3504))
- Being unable to use `data` as an instruction parameter ([#3574](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3574))

## SPL

### New Token 2022 instructions

The following Token 2022 instructions were added:

- `burn_checked`
- `mint_to_checked`
- `approve_checked`
- `withdraw_withheld_tokens_from_accounts`

## IDL

### Safety comment checks

In v0.30.1, enabling all features in Rust Analyzer would panic because the `idl-build` feature expected an environment variable that `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` sets but Rust Analyzer doesn't:

```text
custom attribute panicked
message: Safety checks failed: Failed to get program path
```

The check is now lenient when the variable is absent.

### `address{:rs}` constraint with non-const expressions

A v0.30 regression caused non-const expressions in the `address{:rs}` constraint to fail to build:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct MyIx {
    #[account(address = my_account.authority())]
    pub authority: Signer<'info>,
    pub my_account: Account<'info, MyAccount>,
}
```

Fixed in [#3216](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3216).

### `Program{:rs}` accounts with full paths

Fully-qualified external program types now work in the accounts struct:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct FullPath<'info> {
    pub external_program: Program<'info, external::program::External>,
}
```

### `IdlBuilder{:rs}`

[`build_idl(){:rs}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.31.0/idl/src/build.rs#L119) couldn't gain new parameters without a breaking change. The new builder API solves that:

```rs showLineNumbers=false
let idl = IdlBuilder::new().program_path(path).skip_lint(true).build()?;
```

See [`IdlBuilder{:rs}`](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang-idl/0.1.2/anchor_lang_idl/build/struct.IdlBuilder.html) for the full API.

### Generation improvements

The following issues with the IDL generation have been fixed:

- A bug where using tuple parameters in instructions would result in an incorrect IDL ([#3294](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3294))
- A bug where doc comments could trigger false-positives during module paths conversion ([#3359](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3359))
- A bug where the generated IDL only has partial resolution information ([#3474](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3474))
- Being unable to use constant identifiers as generic arguments ([#3522](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3522))
- Being unable to pass in a `Pubkey{:rs}` constant to `seeds::program{:rs}` ([#3559](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3559))
- Being unable to pass in an account or an argument to `seeds::program{:rs}` ([#3570](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3570))

## TypeScript

### Simpler `Program{:ts}` construction

TypeScript's structural inference of JSON imports made the `Program{:ts}` constructor awkward to call without an extra cast:

```ts showLineNumbers=false
import * as idl from './idl/my_program.json'
import type { MyProgram } from './types/my_program'

const program = new Program(idl as unknown as MyProgram, provider)
```

The constructor no longer infers the IDL type from its `idl{:ts}` argument, so the explicit type parameter is honored without casting:

```ts showLineNumbers=false
const program = new Program<MyProgram>(idl, provider)
```

### Error improvements

Account resolution error now includes the accounts that weren't able to get resolved:

```text
Reached maximum depth for account resolution. Unresolved accounts: `pda`, `anotherPda`
```

Similarly, unsupported `view` method error now includes the possible causes:

```text
Error: Method does not support views. The instruction should return a value, and its accounts must be read-only
```

### Type improvements

Tests commonly reached for `// @ts-ignore{:ts}` to access the payer keypair:

```ts showLineNumbers=false
// @ts-ignore
const payer = program.provider.wallet.payer
```

The `Provider{:ts}` interface now declares an optional `wallet?: Wallet{:ts}` field, and `Wallet{:ts}` declares an optional `payer?: Keypair{:ts}` field. The non-null assertion (`!`) replaces the suppression in test code, where these fields are guaranteed:

```ts showLineNumbers=false
const payer = program.provider.wallet!.payer!
```

### Better confirmation

`Provider.sendAndConfirm(){:ts}` now accepts an optional `blockhash{:ts}` for more reliable confirmation:

```ts showLineNumbers=false
await program.provider.sendAndConfirm(tx, signers, { blockhash: ... });
```

### Programs with numbers in their name

`anchor.workspace{:ts}` now resolves programs whose names contain digits in every casing scenario. See [#3450](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/pull/3450) for the full breakdown.

## Rust client

### `tokio` support

[`anchor-client`](https://docs.rs/anchor-client/0.31.0/anchor_client/index.html) is now compatible with `tokio` when the `async` feature is enabled. See the [`tokio` example](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.31.0/client/example/src/nonblocking.rs#L65-L99).

### Mock client

Enabling the `mock` feature lets tests pass in a [mock RPC client](https://docs.rs/solana-client/2.1.0/solana_client/rpc_client/struct.RpcClient.html#method.new_mock):

```toml
anchor-client = { version = "0.31.0", features = ["mock"] }
```

See the full list of notable changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.31.0/CHANGELOG.md#0310---2025-03-08).

# 0-31-1.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/updates/release-notes/0-31-1.mdx

title: 0.31.1
description: Anchor release notes for 0.31.1.

`0.31.1` is a patch release that fixes `proc-macro2`-related IDL build errors (see [`proc-macro2` build fix](#proc-macro2-build-fix)). Future Anchor releases will be published under the `solanafoundation` GitHub organization.

## How to upgrade

1. Update `anchor-cli`:

   ```bash
   $ <blue>avm</blue> install 0.31.1
   ```

2. Update Anchor crate(s) to `0.31.1`.

3. Update TS package(s) to `0.31.1`.

## Recommended Solana version

The recommended Solana version is `2.1.0`, the same as [v0.31.0's Recommended Solana Version](./0-31-0#recommended-solana-version).

## Docker

Docker images have moved to [`solanafoundation/anchor`](https://hub.docker.com/r/solanafoundation/anchor) on Docker Hub. All future images will be published under that namespace.

## IDL

### `proc-macro2` build fix

`proc-macro2 1.0.95` removed the `source_file(){:rs}` method on `Span{:rs}` to track an upstream nightly change ([rust-lang/rust#139671](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/139671)). The removal surfaced as a build error in earlier Anchor versions:

```text
error[E0599]: no method named `source_file` found for struct `proc_macro2::Span` in the current scope
```

The IDL build now compiles against `proc-macro2 >= 1.0.95`.

## TypeScript

### Account resolver no longer requires wallet

Signer resolution previously required a `wallet{:ts}` field on the `Provider{:ts}` implementor, failing with:

```text
This function requires the `Provider` interface implementor to have a `wallet` field.
```

The resolver now only requires `Provider.publicKey{:ts}`.

### Multiple constant generics

Multiple constant generics on a type no longer trigger parsing errors.

See the full list of notable changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.31.1/CHANGELOG.md#0311---2025-04-19).

# 0-32-0.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/updates/release-notes/0-32-0.mdx

title: 0.32.0
description: Anchor release notes for 0.32.0.

`0.32.0` is the last planned release before the breaking changes that stabilize Anchor `1.0`. These notes cover the most significant changes; the full list lives in the [`CHANGELOG.md{:file}`](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.32.0/CHANGELOG.md#0320---2025-10-08).

## How to upgrade

1. Update `anchor-cli`:

   ```bash
   <blue>avm</blue> install 0.32.0
   ```

2. Update Anchor crate(s) to `0.32.0`.

3. Update TS package(s) to `0.32.0`.

## Recommended Solana version

The recommended Solana version is `2.3.0`. Install the new tooling with:

```console
$ <blue>sh</blue> <dim>-c</dim> "$(curl <dim>-sSfL</dim> https://release.anza.xyz/v2.3.0/install)"
```

## CLI

### `<blue>anchor</blue> verify` switches to `solana-verify`

Anchor versions before `0.32.0` produced verifiable builds using the `solanafoundation/anchor` Docker image. `0.32.0` replaces that pipeline with [`solana-verify`](https://github.com/Ellipsis-Labs/solana-verifiable-build) under the hood. The user-facing entry point is unchanged: `$ <blue>anchor</blue> verify` still produces and verifies builds. Verifying a build produced by Anchor `< 0.32.0` with the new CLI is expected to fail because the verification mechanism has changed.

### IDL upload by default on deploy

`$ <blue>anchor</blue> deploy` now uploads the IDL on every deployment by default. Pass `<dim>--no-idl</dim>` to deploy the program without touching the on-chain IDL.

### Minimum Rust version raised to `1.89.0`

IDL builds now require Rust `1.89.0` or higher because earlier Rust versions don't expose the stabilized [`Span::local_file(){:rs}`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/proc_macro/struct.Span.html#method.local_file). Update the toolchain with:

```console
$ <blue>rustup</blue> update
```

Confirm the installed version with:

```console
$ <blue>rustc</blue> <dim>--version</dim>
```

This is the host Rust toolchain, distinct from the forked `rustc` that the Solana platform tools use to compile programs.

## IDL

### IDL building is now stabilized

With [`Span::local_file(){:rs}`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/proc_macro/struct.Span.html#method.local_file) stabilized, IDLs build against the current stable Rust compiler instead of nightly. That removes a class of upstream-nightly breakages that previously surfaced as build errors on `0.31.0` and earlier:

```text
no method named source_file found for struct proc_macro2::Span in the current
scope
```

## Lang

### Better error message for `init` on `SystemAccount{:rs}`

`init`-ing a `SystemAccount{:rs}` previously surfaced as a confusing missing-crate error:

```text
error[E0425]: cannot find crate `try_from_unchecked` in the list of imported crates
error[E0425]: cannot find crate `try_from` in the list of imported crates
```

The compile-time error now explains the actual constraint and suggests an alternative:

```text
Cannot use `init` on a `SystemAccount`.
The `SystemAccount` type represents an already-existing account
owned by the system program and cannot be initialized.
If you need to create a new account, use a more specific account type
or `UncheckedAccount` and perform manual initialization instead.
```

### Use `solana-invoke` instead of `solana_cpi::invoke{:rs}` for CPI

`solana_cpi::invoke{:rs}` from `solana-program` is heavier on compute units than necessary. Replacing it with `solana-invoke` saves an average of 5% CUs across CPI call sites in Anchor programs.

### Solang is no longer supported

Solang templates are no longer bundled with Anchor. Projects that want to keep using Solang must build with [Solang's standalone tooling](https://github.com/hyperledger-solang/solang?tab=readme-ov-file).

## TypeScript

### Remove event parsing panic issues

A maliciously crafted event could previously panic the TS event parser. The parser's regex has been hardened to fail closed instead of panicking.

### Added support for `bun` as a package manager

`bun` joins `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm` as a recognized value for `toolchain.package_manager` in `Anchor.toml{:file}`:

```toml
[toolchain]
package_manager = "bun"
```

The same value is accepted when scaffolding a new workspace:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim><NAME></dim> <dim>--package-manager</dim> bun
```

The default remains `yarn`.

See the full list of notable changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/v0.32.0/CHANGELOG.md#0320---2025-10-08).
