# account-constraints.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/reference/account-constraints.mdx

title: Account constraints
description: 'Reference for Anchor account constraints used inside the `#[account(...)]{:rs}` attribute.'

Account constraints are declared inside the `#[account(...)]{:rs}` attribute on fields of a struct that derives [`Accounts{:rs}`](https://docs.rs/anchor-lang/latest/anchor_lang/derive.Accounts.html). They run before the instruction handler and reject the transaction if any check fails.

See the [constraint codegen](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/62865c636aecc6974fc9cfebfc6cf08ca4f0bb72/lang/syn/src/codegen/accounts/constraints.rs) for implementation details.

<Callout variant="notation" title="Custom error syntax">
  Each constraint accepts an optional `@ <custom_error>{:rs}` clause to override the default error. Wherever you see `@ <custom_error>{:rs}` in the snippets below, the constraint will return that variant instead of Anchor's built-in error code on failure.
</Callout>

## Normal constraints

### `#[account(signer)]{:rs}`

Checks the given account signed the transaction. Prefer the `Signer{:rs}` type if `signer{:rs}` is the only constraint needed on the account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(signer)]
#[account(signer @ <custom_error>)]
```

### `#[account(mut)]{:rs}`

Checks the given account is mutable and persists any state changes after the instruction completes:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(mut)]
#[account(mut @ <custom_error>)]
```

### `#[account(dup)]{:rs}`

Allows a mutable account to be passed in more than once. Anchor blocks duplicate mutable accounts by default to avoid silent overwrites; `dup{:rs}` opts back in when the duplication is intentional.

<Callout variant="note">
  This constraint only applies to mutable account types that serialize on exit. `UncheckedAccount{:rs}`, `Signer{:rs}`, `SystemAccount{:rs}`, `AccountLoader{:rs}`, `Program{:rs}`, and `Interface{:rs}` allow duplicates already because they don't serialize data on exit.
</Callout>

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(mut, dup)]
#[account(mut, dup @ <custom_error>)]
```

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct AllowsDuplicateMutable<'info> {
    #[account(mut)]
    pub account1: Account<'info, Counter>,
    // This account can be the same as account1
    #[account(mut, dup)]
    pub account2: Account<'info, Counter>,
}

pub fn allows_duplicate_mutable(ctx: Context<AllowsDuplicateMutable>) -> Result<()> {
    Ok(())
}
```

### `#[account(init)]{:rs}`

Creates the account via a CPI to the System Program and writes the 8-byte account discriminator. Requires `payer{:rs}` and `space{:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    init,
    payer = <target_account>,
    space = <num_bytes>
)]
```

### `#[account(init_if_needed)]{:rs}`

Same as `init{:rs}` but only runs if the account does not exist yet. Requires the `init-if-needed` cargo feature:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    init_if_needed,
    payer = <target_account>
)]

#[account(
    init_if_needed,
    payer = <target_account>,
    space = <num_bytes>
)]
```

### `#[account(seeds, bump)]{:rs}`

Checks that the given account is a PDA derived from the currently executing program, the seeds, and (if provided) the bump. See [Program derived address](/docs/v1/fundamentals/pdas/) for usage patterns:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    seeds = <seeds>,
    bump
)]

#[account(
    seeds = <seeds>,
    bump,
    seeds::program = <expr>
)]

#[account(
    seeds = <seeds>,
    bump = <expr>
)]

#[account(
    seeds = <seeds>,
    bump = <expr>,
    seeds::program = <expr>
)]
```

### `#[account(has_one = target)]{:rs}`

Checks that the `target{:rs}` field stored on the account matches the key of the `target{:rs}` field in the `Accounts{:rs}` struct:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    has_one = <target_account>
)]

#[account(
    has_one = <target_account> @ <custom_error>
)]
```

### `#[account(address = expr)]{:rs}`

Checks the account key matches the given pubkey:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(address = <expr>)]
#[account(address = <expr> @ <custom_error>)]
```

### `#[account(owner = expr)]{:rs}`

Checks the account owner matches `expr{:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(owner = <expr>)]
#[account(owner = <expr> @ <custom_error>)]
```

### `#[account(executable)]{:rs}`

Checks the account is executable (the account is a program):

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(executable)]
```

### `#[account(zero)]{:rs}`

Checks the account discriminator is zero. Use for accounts larger than 10 KiB, where `init{:rs}` exceeds the System Program's allocation limit:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(zero)]
```

### `#[account(close = target)]{:rs}`

Closes the account by sending its lamports to `target{:rs}` and zeroing its data:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(close = <target_account>)]
```

### `#[account(constraint = expr)]{:rs}`

Custom constraint that checks whether the given expression evaluates to `true{:rs}`:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(constraint = <expr>)]
#[account(
    constraint = <expr> @ <custom_error>
)]
```

### `#[account(realloc)]{:rs}`

Reallocates program account space at the start of an instruction. `realloc::zero{:rs}` controls whether new bytes are zeroed:

If the change is additive, lamports are transferred from `realloc::payer{:rs}`
to maintain rent exemption. If the change is subtractive, all lamports above
the new rent-exempt minimum are transferred back to `realloc::payer{:rs}`.

Warning: Do not use subtractive realloc on accounts that intentionally hold
extra lamports, such as vaults. Those extra lamports will also be transferred
to `realloc::payer{:rs}`; the current v1 behavior does not limit refunds to
rent savings alone.

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    realloc = <space>,
    realloc::payer = <target>,
    realloc::zero = <bool>
)]
```

### `#[account(discriminator = <expr>)]{:rs}`

Overrides the auto-generated discriminator for an account. Any constant expression is accepted. All-zero discriminators are rejected because zeroed discriminators are indistinguishable from newly allocated accounts; see [zeroed discriminators](/docs/v1/security/footguns/#zeroed-discriminators) for the security background:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(discriminator = 12)]
#[account(discriminator = [1, 2, 3, 4])]
#[account(discriminator = MY_CONST_DISCRIMINATOR)]
```

## SPL constraints

### `#[account(token::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates token accounts with the specified mint and authority:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    token::mint = <target_account>,
    token::authority = <target_account>
)]

#[account(
    token::mint = <target_account>,
    token::authority = <target_account>,
    token::token_program = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(mint::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates mint accounts with the specified parameters:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    mint::authority = <target_account>,
    mint::decimals = <expr>
)]

#[account(
    mint::authority = <target_account>,
    mint::decimals = <expr>,
    mint::freeze_authority = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(associated_token::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates associated token accounts:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    associated_token::mint = <target_account>,
    associated_token::authority = <target_account>
)]

#[account(
    associated_token::mint = <target_account>,
    associated_token::authority = <target_account>,
    associated_token::token_program = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(*::token_program = expr)]{:rs}`

Overrides the token program used by `token{:rs}`, `mint{:rs}`, or `associated_token{:rs}` constraints:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(*::token_program = <target_account>)]
```

## Token extensions constraints

### `#[account(extensions::close_authority::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates the close authority extension on the mint account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    extensions::close_authority::authority = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(extensions::permanent_delegate::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates the permanent delegate extension on the mint account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    extensions::permanent_delegate::delegate = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(extensions::transfer_hook::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates the transfer hook extension on the mint account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    extensions::transfer_hook::authority = <target_account>,
    extensions::transfer_hook::program_id = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(extensions::group_pointer::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates the group pointer extension on the mint account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    extensions::group_pointer::authority = <target_account>,
    extensions::group_pointer::group_address = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(extensions::group_member_pointer::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates the group member pointer extension on the mint account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    extensions::group_member_pointer::authority = <target_account>,
    extensions::group_member_pointer::member_address = <target_account>
)]
```

### `#[account(extensions::metadata_pointer::*)]{:rs}`

Creates or validates the metadata pointer extension on the mint account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(
    extensions::metadata_pointer::authority = <target_account>,
    extensions::metadata_pointer::metadata_address = <target_account>
)]
```

## Instruction attribute

### `#[instruction(...)]{:rs}`

Exposes the instruction's arguments to the `Accounts{:rs}` struct so constraints can reference them. The example below uses `input{:rs}` in the `space{:rs}` calculation when initializing an account:

```rust showLineNumbers=false {8}
#[program]
pub mod example {
    use super::*;

    pub fn initialize(ctx: Context<Initialize>, input: String) -> Result<()> {
        // --snip--
    }
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
#[instruction(input: String)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    #[account(
        init,
        payer = signer,
        space = 8 + 4 + input.len(),
    )]
    pub new_account: Account<'info, DataAccount>,
    // --snip--
}
```

Arguments must appear in the same order as the handler signature. Listing every argument is valid:

```rust showLineNumbers=false {10}
#[program]
pub mod example {
    use super::*;

    pub fn initialize(ctx: Context<Initialize>, input_one: String, input_two: String) -> Result<()> {
        // --snip--
    }
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
#[instruction(input_one: String, input_two: String)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    // --snip--
}
```

Omitting trailing arguments is valid:

```rust showLineNumbers=false {10}
#[program]
pub mod example {
    use super::*;

    pub fn initialize(ctx: Context<Initialize>, input_one: String, input_two: String) -> Result<()> {
        // --snip--
    }
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
#[instruction(input_one: String)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    // --snip--
}
```

Skipping a leading argument is invalid and produces a compile error:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[program]
pub mod example {
    use super::*;

    pub fn initialize(ctx: Context<Initialize>, input_one: String, input_two: String) -> Result<()> {
        // --snip--
    }
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
#[instruction(input_two: String)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    // --snip--
}
```

# Accepts kebab-case names...

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/reference/anchor-toml.mdx

title: '`Anchor.toml{:file}` configuration'
description: "Reference for the fields available in an Anchor workspace's `Anchor.toml` file."

`Anchor.toml` configures a workspace's provider, programs, scripts, test validator, and toolchain. The full set of fields is defined in the [`Config` struct](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/blob/master/cli/src/config.rs) in the Anchor CLI.

## `[provider]` (required)

Sets the wallet and cluster used for all `anchor` commands:

```toml
[provider]
cluster = "localnet"                    # The cluster used for all commands.
wallet = "~/.config/solana/id.json"     # The keypair used for all commands.
```

## `[scripts]` (required for testing)

Defines named scripts runnable with `$ <blue>anchor</blue> run <script>`. The `test` script is executed by `$ <blue>anchor</blue> test`:

```toml
[scripts]
test = "yarn run ts-mocha -p ./tsconfig.json -t 1000000 tests/**/*.ts"
```

## `skip_local_validator`

When set to `true`, `$ <blue>anchor</blue> test` does not start a local validator for localnet tests. `$ <blue>anchor</blue> init` writes this for Rust templates that run the Solana VM in-process, such as LiteSVM and Mollusk:

```toml
skip_local_validator = true
```

## `[features]`

### `resolution`

Enables IDL account resolution. Defaults to `true`:

```toml
[features]
resolution = true
```

## `[workspace]`

### `types`

Copies the generated `<idl>.ts{:file}` file to the given directory on `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build`. Useful for committing the IDL types into a frontend that does not have access to the `target{:dir}` directory:

```toml
[workspace]
types = "app/src/idl/"
```

### `members`

Paths (relative to `Anchor.toml{:file}`) to every `Cargo.toml{:file}` manifest the `anchor` CLI should compile. Programs using the standard Anchor workflow can omit this field; non-Anchor programs that still publish through the CLI must list their manifests here:

```toml
[workspace]
members = [
    "programs/*",
    "other_place/my_program"
]
```

### `exclude`

Lists workspace paths to skip, mirroring the include list in `members`:

```toml
[workspace]
exclude = [
    "programs/my_program"
]
```

## `[programs]`

Maps program names to addresses, scoped by cluster:

```toml
[programs.localnet]
my_program = "Fg6PaFpoGXkYsidMpWTK6W2BeZ7FEfcYkg476zPFsLnS"
```

During tests on localnet, Anchor reads `programs.localnet` to tell `solana-test-validator` which programs to load at genesis via `--bpf-program`.

## `[clients]`

Configures [Codama](https://github.com/codama-idl/codama) client generation. When `auto = true`, `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` converts emitted Anchor IDLs into Codama IDLs and invokes the selected language renderers after the build completes.

Each language can be enabled with a boolean or a table. If `path` is omitted, the default output directory is `clients/<language>{:dir}`. Supported language keys are `js`, `js-umi`, `rust`, and `go`:

```toml
[clients]
auto = true
rust = true
js = { enable = true }
go = { enable = true, path = "go-client" }
js-umi = false
```

## `[test]`

### `startup_wait`

Increases the time `anchor` waits for `solana-test-validator` to start. Useful when cloning many accounts (see [`test.validator.clone`](#testvalidatorclone)) extends startup time:

```toml
[test]
startup_wait = 10000
```

### `genesis`

Starts `solana-test-validator` with the listed programs preloaded:

```toml
[[test.genesis]]
address = "srmqPvymJeFKQ4zGQed1GFppgkRHL9kaELCbyksJtPX"
program = "dex.so"

[[test.genesis]]
address = "22Y43yTVxuUkoRKdm9thyRhQ3SdgQS7c7kB6UNCiaczD"
program = "swap.so"
upgradeable = true
```

### `upgradeable`

Deploys the program-under-test with `--upgradeable-program` so tests can exercise instructions gated on the upgrade authority. The initial upgrade authority is set to `provider.wallet`.

When unset or `false`, the program is deployed with `--bpf-program` and cannot be upgraded:

```toml
[test]
upgradeable = true
```

## `[test.validator]`

Forwards options to `solana-test-validator` (run `$ <blue>solana-test-validator</blue> --help` for the full list) during commands like `$ <blue>anchor</blue> test`:

```toml
[test.validator]
url = "https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com"     # This is the url of the cluster that accounts are cloned from (See `test.validator.clone`).
warp_slot = 1337                                # Warp the ledger to `warp_slot` after starting the validator.
slots_per_epoch = 5                             # Override the number of slots in an epoch.
rpc_port = 1337                                 # Set JSON RPC on this port, and the next port for the RPC websocket.
limit_ledger_size = 1337                        # Keep this amount of shreds in root slots.
ledger = "test-ledger"                          # Set ledger location.
gossip_port = 1337                              # Gossip port number for the validator.
gossip_host = "127.0.0.1"                       # Gossip DNS name or IP address for the validator to advertise in gossip.
faucet_sol = 1337                               # Give the faucet address this much SOL in genesis.
faucet_port = 1337                              # Enable the faucet on this port.
dynamic_port_range = "1337 - 13337"             # Range to use for dynamically assigned ports.
bind_address = "127.0.0.1"                      # IP address to bind the validator ports.
```

### `test.validator.clone`

Clones an account from `test.validator.url` into the test cluster. If `address` points to a program owned by the BPF upgradeable loader, Anchor (>= 0.23.0) clones the program data account automatically:

```toml
[test.validator]
url = "https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com"

[[test.validator.clone]]
address = "7NL2qWArf2BbEBBH1vTRZCsoNqFATTddH6h8GkVvrLpG"
[[test.validator.clone]]
address = "2RaN5auQwMdg5efgCaVqpETBV8sacWGR8tkK4m9kjo5r"
[[test.validator.clone]]
address = "metaqbxxUerdq28cj1RbAWkYQm3ybzjb6a8bt518x1s" # implicitly also clones PwDiXFxQsGra4sFFTT8r1QWRMd4vfumiWC1jfWNfdYT
```

### `test.validator.account`

Uploads an account from a `.json` file:

```toml
[[test.validator.account]]
address = "Ev8WSPQsGb4wfjybqff5eZNcS3n6HaMsBkMk9suAiuM"
filename = "some_account.json"

[[test.validator.account]]
address = "Ev8WSPQsGb4wfjybqff5eZNcS3n6HaMsBkMk9suAiuM"
filename = "some_other_account.json"
```

## `[surfpool]`

Configures the [Surfpool](https://github.com/solana-foundation/surfpool) validator, used when `$ <blue>anchor</blue> test <dim>--validator</dim> <dim>surfpool</dim>` selects Surfpool as the local network backend. Surfpool is a lightweight Solana simulator with features like automatic account cloning and runbook execution. All fields are optional and have sensible defaults:

```toml
[surfpool]
startup_wait = 5000                                # Time (ms) to wait for Surfpool to start. Default: 5000.
shutdown_wait = 2000                               # Time (ms) to wait for Surfpool to shut down. Default: 2000.
rpc_port = 8899                                    # JSON RPC port. Default: 8899.
ws_port = 8900                                     # WebSocket port. If not set, derived automatically.
host = "127.0.0.1"                                 # IP address to bind to. Default: "127.0.0.1".
online = true                                      # Enable online mode (clone accounts from a remote cluster).
datasource_rpc_url = "https://api.mainnet.solana.com"
airdrop_addresses = ["addr1...", "addr2..."]       # Addresses to airdrop SOL to at startup.
manifest_file_path = "./Cargo.toml"                # Path to the Cargo.toml manifest file.
runbooks = ["./runbooks/setup.json"]               # Paths to runbook files to execute on startup.
slot_time = 400                                    # Simulated slot time in milliseconds.
log_level = "info"                                 # Log level for Surfpool. Default: "none".
block_production_mode = "clock"                    # Block production mode. Default: "transaction".
```

### `startup_wait`

Time in milliseconds to wait for Surfpool to start up. Useful when loading many accounts or running runbooks at startup. Default: `5000`.

### `shutdown_wait`

Time in milliseconds to wait for Surfpool to shut down gracefully. Default: `2000`.

### `rpc_port`

The port on which Surfpool exposes its JSON RPC endpoint. Default: `8899`.

### `ws_port`

The port for the WebSocket endpoint. If not specified, it is derived automatically.

### `host`

The IP address to bind the Surfpool validator ports to. Default: `"127.0.0.1"`.

### `online`

When set to `true`, Surfpool operates in online mode, cloning accounts from the remote cluster specified by `datasource_rpc_url`. Default: `false`.

### `datasource_rpc_url`

The RPC URL of the remote cluster used as a data source when `online` is enabled:

```toml
[surfpool]
online = true
datasource_rpc_url = "https://api.mainnet.solana.com"
```

### `airdrop_addresses`

A list of base58-encoded addresses that will receive an airdrop of SOL when Surfpool starts:

```toml
[surfpool]
airdrop_addresses = [
    "Fg6PaFpoGXkYsidMpWTK6W2BeZ7FEfcYkg476zPFsLnS",
    "7NL2qWArf2BbEBBH1vTRZCsoNqFATTddH6h8GkVvrLpG",
]
```

### `manifest_file_path`

Path to the `Cargo.toml{:file}` manifest file for the workspace. Typically not needed because Anchor resolves it automatically.

### `runbooks`

A list of file paths to runbooks that Surfpool will execute on startup. Runbooks allow setting up initial state (deploy programs, create accounts, etc.) before tests run:

```toml
[surfpool]
runbooks = ["./runbooks/setup.json"]
```

### `slot_time`

The simulated slot time in milliseconds. Controls how fast slots advance in the Surfpool simulator.

### `log_level`

Log verbosity for the Surfpool process. Common values include `"none"`, `"info"`, `"debug"`, `"warn"`, and `"error"`. Default: `"none"`.

### `block_production_mode`

Controls how Surfpool produces blocks. Default: `"transaction"`. Known values:

- `"clock"` produces blocks at regular intervals based on `slot_time`.
- `"transaction"` produces a new block for each incoming transaction.

```toml
[surfpool]
block_production_mode = "clock"
```

## `[toolchain]`

Overrides toolchain versions for the workspace, similar to [`rust-toolchain.toml{:file}`](https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/overrides.html#the-toolchain-file):

```toml
[toolchain]
anchor_version = "1.0.1"    # `anchor-cli` version to use (requires `avm`)
solana_version = "3.1.10"   # Solana version to use (applies to all Solana tools)
package_manager = "yarn"    # JS package manager to use
```

### `package_manager`

Selects the JS package manager Anchor uses for client and workspace commands. Valid values are `npm`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, and `bun`.

When the field is omitted, Anchor probes `pnpm`, `yarn`, then `npm` and uses the first one found on `PATH`. Values must be lowercase, since they are deserialized with `serde(rename_all = "lowercase")`:

```toml
[toolchain]
package_manager = "pnpm"
```

### `hooks`

Configures commands that run at specific stages of the build, test, and deploy pipeline:

```toml
[hooks]
# Accepts kebab-case names...
pre-build = "echo foo"
# ...and snake-case names
post_build = "echo bar"
# Accepts a list of commands, run in series
pre-test = ["echo 1", "echo 2"]
# Non-zero exit codes will abort the CLI
post-test = "exit 1"
# Unused hooks may be omitted
# pre-deploy = []
# post-deploy = []
```

## `[registry]` (removed)

The `[registry]` section is no longer supported and was removed in `1.0.0`. Remove it from any existing `Anchor.toml`:

```toml title="Anchor.toml" del={1-2}
[registry]
url = "https://anchor.projectserum.com"
```

# avm.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/reference/avm.mdx

title: Anchor version manager
description: Manage multiple installations of the anchor-cli binary.

Anchor Version Manager (`$ <blue>avm</blue>`) manages multiple installations of the `anchor-cli` binary. Use it to switch between versions for verifiable builds or to work with an alternate release:

```console
$ <blue>avm</blue> <dim>--help</dim>
Anchor version manager

<bold>Usage:</bold> <bold>avm</bold> <COMMAND>

<bold>Commands:</bold>
  <bold>use</bold>          Use a specific version of Anchor
  <bold>install</bold>      Install a version of Anchor
  <bold>uninstall</bold>    Uninstall a version of Anchor
  <bold>list</bold>         List available versions of Anchor
  <bold>update</bold>       Update to the latest Anchor version
  <bold>self-update</bold>  Update avm itself to the latest version via cargo install
  <bold>completions</bold>  Generate shell completions for AVM
  <bold>help</bold>         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

<bold>Options:</bold>
  <bold>-h</bold>, <bold>--help</bold>     Print help
  <bold>-V</bold>, <bold>--version</bold>  Print version
```

## `<blue>avm</blue> install`

Install a version of `anchor-cli` with `$ <blue>avm</blue> install <dim><version-or-commit></dim>`. The version argument follows semver, or pass `latest` for the latest stable release and `latest-pre-release` for the latest pre-release:

```console
$ <blue>avm</blue> install latest
$ <blue>avm</blue> install latest-pre-release
```

You can also install with the following arguments:

| Argument example | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `$ <blue>avm</blue> install 1.0.0-rc.3` | Install specific pre-release tag |
| `$ <blue>avm</blue> install 0.30.1-cfe82aa682138f7c6c58bf7a78f48f7d63e9e466` | Install a `<dim><version></dim>`-`<dim><commit></dim>` pair |
| `$ <blue>avm</blue> install cfe82aa682138f7c6c58bf7a78f48f7d63e9e466` | Install by full commit hash |
| `$ <blue>avm</blue> install cfe82aa` | Install by short commit hash |

## `<blue>avm</blue> list`

List installed and available versions with `$ <blue>avm</blue> list`. Pass `--pre-release` to include pre-release versions:

```console
<blue>avm</blue> list <dim>--pre-release</dim>
```

## `<blue>avm</blue> uninstall`

Remove an installed version with `$ <blue>avm</blue> uninstall <version>`.

## `<blue>avm</blue> update`

Update to the latest stable version with `$ <blue>avm</blue> update`. Pass `<dim>--pre-release</dim>` to update to the latest pre-release instead:

```console
<blue>avm</blue> update <dim>--pre-release</dim>
```

## `<blue>avm</blue> use`

Select an installed version with `$ <blue>avm</blue> use <dim><version></dim>`. The selected version remains active until the command runs again with a different argument. As with `$ <blue>avm</blue> install`, the version argument accepts `latest` or `latest-pre-release`:

```console
<blue>avm</blue> use latest
<blue>avm</blue> use latest-pre-release
```

## `<blue>avm</blue> self-update`

Update `$ <blue>avm</blue>` itself with `$ <blue>avm</blue> self-update`. By default this installs the latest stable release of `$ <blue>avm</blue>`.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<dim>--pre-release</dim>` | Update to the latest pre-release version instead of the latest stable |
| `<dim>--bleeding-edge</dim>` | Build and install from the latest commit on the master branch (conflicts with `<dim>--pre-release</dim>`) |

```console
$ <blue>avm</blue> self-update
$ <blue>avm</blue> self-update <dim>--pre-release</dim>
$ <blue>avm</blue> self-update <dim>--bleeding-edge</dim>
```

`$ <blue>avm</blue>` also passively warns you when it detects that a newer version of itself is available.

# cli.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/reference/cli.mdx

title: Anchor CLI
description: Anchor CLI reference documentation.

The Anchor CLI manages an Anchor workspace: scaffolding projects, building programs, deploying to a cluster, running tests, and interacting with on-chain IDLs. Run `$ <blue>anchor</blue> <dim>--help</dim>` on any subcommand for the full list of flags:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> <dim>--help</dim>
<bold>Usage:</bold> <bold>anchor-1.0.1</bold> [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

<bold>Commands:</bold>
  <bold>init</bold>          Initializes a workspace
  <bold>build</bold>         Builds the workspace
  <bold>expand</bold>        Expands macros (wrapper around cargo expand)
  <bold>verify</bold>        Verifies the on-chain bytecode matches the locally compiled artifact. Run this command inside a program subdirectory, i.e., in the dir containing the program's Cargo.toml
  <bold>test</bold>          Runs integration tests
  <bold>new</bold>           Creates a new program
  <bold>idl</bold>           Commands for interacting with interface definitions
  <bold>clean</bold>         Remove all artifacts from the generated directories except program keypairs
  <bold>migrate</bold>       Runs the deploy migration script
  <bold>airdrop</bold>       Request an airdrop of SOL
  <bold>cluster</bold>       Cluster commands
  <bold>config</bold>        Configuration management commands
  <bold>shell</bold>         Starts a node shell with an Anchor client setup according to the local config
  <bold>run</bold>           Runs the script defined by the current workspace's Anchor.toml
  <bold>keys</bold>          Program keypair commands
  <bold>localnet</bold>      Localnet commands
  <bold>account</bold>       Fetch and deserialize an account using the IDL provided
  <bold>completions</bold>   Generates shell completions
  <bold>address</bold>       Get your public key
  <bold>balance</bold>       Get your balance
  <bold>epoch</bold>         Get current epoch
  <bold>epoch-info</bold>    Get information about the current epoch
  <bold>logs</bold>          Stream transaction logs
  <bold>show-account</bold>  Show the contents of an account
  <bold>keygen</bold>        Keypair generation and management
  <bold>program</bold>       Program deployment and management commands
  <bold>help</bold>          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

<bold>Options:</bold>
      <bold>--provider.cluster</bold> <CLUSTER>  Cluster override
      <bold>--provider.wallet</bold> <WALLET>    Wallet override
      <bold>--commitment</bold> <COMMITMENT>     Commitment override (valid values: processed, confirmed, finalized)
  <bold>-h</bold>, <bold>--help</bold>                        Print help
  <bold>-V</bold>, <bold>--version</bold>                     Print version
```

## `<blue>anchor</blue> account`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> account <dim><program-name></dim>.<dim><AccountTypeName></dim> <dim><account-pubkey></dim>
```

Fetches an account with the given public key and deserializes the data to JSON using the type name provided. When run inside a workspace, the workspace's IDL files supply the data types. Otherwise, an IDL file path must be provided.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<dim><program-name></dim>` | The name of the program where the account struct resides, usually under `programs/<program-name>/{:dir}`. Case-sensitive, exactly matching the folder name (typically kebab-case). |
| `<dim><AccountTypeName></dim>` | The name of the account struct, usually in PascalCase. |
| `<dim><account-pubkey></dim>` | The Pubkey of the account to deserialize, in Base58. |

For example, `$ <blue>anchor</blue> account anchor-escrow.EscrowAccount 3PNkzWKXCsbjijbasnx55NEpJe8DFXvEEbJKdRKpDcfK` deserializes the account at the given pubkey using the `EscrowAccount` struct defined in the `anchor-escrow` program:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> account <dim><program-name></dim>.<dim><AccountTypeName></dim> <dim><account-pubkey></dim> <dim>--idl</dim> <dim><path/to/idl.json></dim>
```

Pass `<dim>--idl</dim>` to deserialize using a specific IDL file even when inside a workspace.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> build`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build
```

Builds programs in the workspace targeting Solana's BPF runtime and emits IDLs into the `target/idl{:dir}` directory:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--verifiable</dim>
```

Runs the build inside a Docker image so that the output binary is deterministic (assuming a `Cargo.lock{:file}` file is used). This command must be run from within a single crate subdirectory in the workspace, for example `programs/<my-program>/{:dir}`. See [verifiable builds](/docs/v1/security/verifiable-builds/) for details.

<Callout variant="tip" title="Passing arguments to cargo build-sbf">
Forward arguments to the underlying `cargo build-sbf` command with `-- <ARGS>`:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--</dim> <dim>--features</dim> my-feature
```

</Callout>

## Cluster

### `<blue>anchor</blue> cluster list`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> cluster list
```

Lists the cluster endpoints:

```text
Cluster Endpoints:

* Mainnet - https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com
* Devnet  - https://api.devnet.solana.com
* Testnet - https://api.testnet.solana.com
```

## `<blue>anchor</blue> codama`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> codama convert <dim><target/idl/program.json></dim> <dim>--out</dim> <dim><codama-idl.json></dim>
$ <blue>anchor</blue> codama generate <dim>-l</dim> <dim>rust,js</dim> <dim>-p</dim> clients <dim><target/idl/program.json></dim>
```

`convert` translates an Anchor IDL into a [Codama](https://github.com/codama-idl/codama) IDL. `generate` runs the same conversion in-process and then invokes the Codama renderer packages for the requested languages. Supported language values are `js`, `js-umi`, `rust`, and `go`.

Codama client generation can also run automatically after `$ <blue>anchor</blue> build` when `[clients] auto = true` is set in [`Anchor.toml`](/docs/v1/reference/anchor-toml/#clients).

## `<blue>anchor</blue> coverage`

```console
$ <blue>cd</blue> programs/<dim><program-name></dim>
$ <blue>anchor</blue> coverage [<dim>--skip-run</dim>] [<dim>--skip-build</dim>] [<dim>--output</dim> <dim>target/coverage/sbf.lcov</dim>]
```

Generates LCOV source coverage from SBF register traces. Run from inside a program directory unless `<dim>--trace-dir</dim>` points at an existing trace set. By default traces are collected under `target/coverage/traces{:dir}`. Pass `<dim>--skip-run</dim>` to generate coverage from existing traces.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> debugger`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> debugger [<dim><test-name></dim>] [<dim>--skip-run</dim>] [<dim>--skip-build</dim>] [<dim>--gdb</dim>]
```

Runs tests with profiling enabled and opens an instruction-level TUI over the captured SBF traces. `<dim>--skip-run</dim>` reuses existing traces, and `<dim>--gdb</dim>` captures through the sbpf gdb-stub trace path (which is much slower).

## `<blue>anchor</blue> deploy`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> deploy
```

Deploys all programs in the workspace to the configured cluster.

<Callout variant="tip" title="Different from solana program deploy">
  Each invocation of `$ <blue>anchor</blue> deploy` generates a *new* program address. To upgrade an
  existing program, use `$ <blue>anchor</blue> upgrade` or `$ <blue>solana</blue> program deploy`
  with the existing program ID.
</Callout>

## `<blue>anchor</blue> expand`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> expand
```

Expands the macros of the program when run inside a program folder, or the entire workspace when run from the workspace root. Pass `<dim>--program-name</dim>` to expand only a specific program.

## IDL

The `idl` subcommand provides commands for interacting with interface definition files. Storing an IDL on chain at a deterministic address (a function of the program's ID) lets clients be generated from nothing but the program ID.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl build`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl build
```

Generates the IDL for the program using the compilation method.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl init`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl init <dim>-f</dim> <dim><target/idl/program.json></dim> <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Creates an IDL account, writing the given `<dim><target/idl/program.json></dim>` file into a program-owned account. By default, the size of the account is double the size of the IDL, leaving room for growth in case the IDL is upgraded later. The `<dim><program-id</dim>` argument is optional. When omitted, `idl.address` from `Anchor.toml{:file}` is used.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl fetch`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl fetch <dim>-o</dim> <dim><out-file.json></dim> <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Fetches an IDL from the configured blockchain. For example, point `Anchor.toml{:file}` at the `mainnet` cluster and run:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl fetch GrAkKfEpTKQuVHG2Y97Y2FF4i7y7Q5AHLK94JBy7Y5yv
```

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl authority`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl authority <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Outputs the IDL account's authority, which is the wallet that has the ability to update the IDL.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl erase-authority`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl erase-authority <dim>-p</dim> <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Erases the IDL account's authority so that upgrades can no longer occur. The configured wallet must be the current authority.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> idl upgrade`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl upgrade <dim>-f</dim> <dim><target/idl/program.json></dim>
```

Upgrades the on-chain IDL to the new `target/idl/program.json{:file}`. The configured wallet must be the current authority. The `program-id` argument is optional. When omitted, `idl.address` is used:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> idl set-authority <dim>-n</dim> <dim><new-authority></dim> <dim>-p</dim> <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Sets a new authority on the IDL account. Both `new-authority` and `program-id` must be encoded in base 58.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> init`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim><project-name></dim>
```

Initializes a project workspace with the following structure:

<FileTree>
  <Dir name="app" comment="Application frontend" />
  <Dir name="migrations">
    <File name="deploy.js" comment="Deploy script" />
  </Dir>
  <Dir name="programs" comment="Solana program crates" />
  <Dir name="tests" comment="JavaScript integration tests" />
  <File name="Anchor.toml" comment="Anchor configuration file" />
  <File name="Cargo.toml" comment="Rust workspace configuration" />
  <File name="package.json" comment="JavaScript dependencies" />
</FileTree>

By default, programs are initialized with a modular structure (multiple files) to promote better code organization. The `<dim>--template</dim>` flag selects a different layout:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim>--template</dim> multiple  <dim># Default: modular structure (recommended)</dim>
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim>--template</dim> single    <dim># Single lib.rs file (for prototyping)</dim>
```

The modular template organizes code into separate files for instructions, state, constants, and errors, making it easier to navigate and maintain as the program grows. See [Anchor.toml](/docs/v1/reference/anchor-toml/) for the full configuration reference.

Pass `<dim>--anchor-version</dim>` to select v1 or v2 Rust templates:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim>--anchor-version</dim> v1  <dim># Default: Anchor v1 Rust templates</dim>
$ <blue>anchor</blue> init <dim>--anchor-version</dim> v2  <dim># Anchor v2 Rust templates</dim>
```

The v2 templates depend on the `anchor-next` git crates until the v2 release is published.

## Keys

Program keypair commands.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> keys list`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> keys list
```

Lists all program keypairs declared in the workspace.

### `<blue>anchor</blue> keys sync`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> keys sync
```

Syncs each program's `declare_id!(){:rs}` value with the actual pubkey of its keypair file.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> migrate`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> migrate
```

Runs the deploy script located at `migrations/deploy.js{:file}`, injecting a provider configured from the workspace's `Anchor.toml{:file}`:

```javascript title="migrations/deploy.js" showLineNumbers=false
const anchor = require('@anchor-lang/core')

module.exports = async function (provider) {
  anchor.setProvider(provider)

  // Add your deploy script here.
}
```

Migrations currently support only this simple deploy script.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> new`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> new <dim><program-name></dim>
```

Creates a new program in the workspace's `programs/{:dir}` directory initialized with boilerplate. By default the modular structure template is used. Pass `<dim>--template</dim>` to select another:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> new <dim>--template</dim> multiple <dim><program-name></dim>  <dim># Default: modular (recommended)</dim>
$ <blue>anchor</blue> new <dim>--template</dim> single <dim><program-name></dim>    <dim># Single file (for prototyping)</dim>
```

Pass `<dim>--anchor-version</dim>` to select v1 or v2 Rust templates:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> new <dim>--anchor-version</dim> v1 <dim><program-name></dim>  <dim># Default: Anchor v1 Rust templates</dim>
$ <blue>anchor</blue> new <dim>--anchor-version</dim> v2 <dim><program-name></dim>  <dim># Anchor v2 Rust templates</dim>
```

## `<blue>anchor</blue> shell`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> shell
```

Starts a Node.js shell with an Anchor client set up according to the local config. The client can interact with deployed programs in the workspace.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> test`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> test
```

Runs an integration test suite against the configured cluster, deploying fresh versions of all workspace programs first.

When the configured network is a localnet, `$ <blue>anchor</blue> test` starts the local network automatically and runs the tests against it. By default, [Surfpool](https://github.com/solana-foundation/surfpool) is used as the local network backend. Pass `<dim>--validator legacy</dim>` to use `solana-test-validator` instead.

<Callout variant="note" title="Local validator conflicts">
`$ <blue>anchor</blue> test` starts its own local validator. Shut down any other local validators first, or the command fails.

To run against a local validator that's already running, pass `<dim>--skip-local-validator</dim>`.

</Callout>

Program logs are streamed to `.anchor/program-logs/<address>.<program-name>.log{:file}` while tests run.

Pass `<dim>--profile</dim>` with Rust/LiteSVM-style tests that enable the generated `profile{:toml}` feature to collect SBF register traces and render flamegraph SVGs under `target/anchor-v2-profile/{:dir}`. Those traces also feed `$ <blue>anchor</blue> debugger` and `$ <blue>anchor</blue> coverage`.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> upgrade`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> upgrade <dim><target/deploy/program.so></dim> <dim>--program-id</dim> <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Uses Solana's upgradeable BPF loader to upgrade the on-chain program code. The configured wallet must be the upgrade authority.

## `<blue>anchor</blue> verify`

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> verify <dim><program-id></dim>
```

Verifies that the on-chain bytecode matches the locally compiled artifact. See [verifiable builds](/docs/v1/security/verifiable-builds/) for the build setup that produces a deterministic binary.

# rust-to-js-types.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/reference/rust-to-js-types.mdx

title: Rust to JS type conversion
description: Reference for how Anchor converts between Rust and TypeScript types in generated clients.

Anchor's generated TypeScript clients map Rust types in the [program IDL](/docs/v1/fundamentals/idl/) to JavaScript values using the rules below. Instruction arguments and account fields follow the same mapping.

## Primitive types

### Booleans

| Rust        | TypeScript     | Example     |
| ----------- | -------------- | ----------- |
| `bool{:rs}` | `boolean{:ts}` | `true{:ts}` |

### Numbers

| Rust | TypeScript | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `u8{:rs}` / `u16{:rs}` / `u32{:rs}` / `i8{:rs}` / `i16{:rs}` / `i32{:rs}` | `number{:ts}` | `99{:ts}` |
| `u64{:rs}` / `u128{:rs}` / `i64{:rs}` / `i128{:rs}` | `anchor.BN{:ts}` | `new anchor.BN(99){:ts}` |
| `f32{:rs}` / `f64{:rs}` | `number{:ts}` | `1.0{:ts}` |

Integers up to 32 bits fit in a JavaScript `number{:ts}`. Wider integers exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER{:ts}`, so Anchor represents them with [`BN{:ts}`](https://github.com/indutny/bn.js) to preserve precision.

### Strings

| Rust          | TypeScript    | Example        |
| ------------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| `String{:rs}` | `string{:ts}` | `"hello"{:ts}` |

## Collections

### Arrays and vectors

| Rust                        | TypeScript      | Example          |
| --------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------- |
| `[T; N]{:rs}` (fixed array) | `Array<T>{:ts}` | `[1, 2, 3]{:ts}` |
| `Vec<T>{:rs}` (vector)      | `Array<T>{:ts}` | `[1, 2, 3]{:ts}` |

### Optional values

| Rust | TypeScript | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Option<T>{:rs}` | `T \| null \| undefined{:ts}` | `null{:ts}` for `None{:rs}`, `42{:ts}` for `Some(42){:rs}` |

## Complex types

### Structs

A Rust struct becomes a TypeScript object type with the same field names:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Rust', 'TypeScript']}>
<Tab>

```rust showLineNumbers=false
struct MyStruct {
    val: u16,
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```ts showLineNumbers=false
type MyStruct = {
  val: number
}

const instance = { val: 99 }
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Enums

A Rust enum becomes an object with a single key matching the active variant. Unit variants carry an empty object, named variants carry an object of fields, and tuple variants carry an array of positional values:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Rust', 'TypeScript']}>
<Tab>

```rust showLineNumbers=false
enum MyEnum {
    One,
    Two { val: u32 },
    Three(u8, i16),
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```ts showLineNumbers=false
// Unit variant
const one = { one: {} }

// Named variant
const two = {
  two: { val: 99 },
}

// Tuple variant
const three = {
  three: [12, -34],
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

# footguns.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/security/footguns.mdx

title: Footguns
description: Common footguns in Anchor that can lead to security or correctness issues.

## Zeroed discriminators

Anchor supports overriding discriminators with custom values for accounts, events, and instructions. All-zero discriminators are only supported on events and instructions. The following forms are rejected for accounts:

```rust showLineNumbers=false
#[account(discriminator = [0, 0, 0])]
#[account(discriminator = 0)]
#[account(discriminator = ZERO_CONSTANT)]
```

<Callout variant="danger" title="Why all-zero account discriminators are rejected">
  An all-zero account discriminator is indistinguishable from a freshly allocated, uninitialized account. A program-owned account whose data is still zero (for example, an `AccountInfo{:rs}` that has been allocated but not yet written, or one prepared for `#[zero]{:rs}` initialization) would pass the discriminator check, exposing the program to takeover via IDL instructions and other security and usability issues.
</Callout>

# sealevel-attacks.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/security/sealevel-attacks.mdx

title: Sealevel attacks
description: A curated list of common Solana security exploits and Anchor-idiomatic fixes from the Sealevel attacks repo.

Anchor eliminates many common footguns, but anything shipped to mainnet should be understood end to end. The [Sealevel attacks repository](https://github.com/coral-xyz/sealevel-attacks) catalogs common exploit patterns. Each entry comes in three variants: an `insecure` version showing the flawed code, a `secure` version with a fix, and a `recommended` version that uses idiomatic Anchor.

<Callout variant="important" title="Not a substitute for review">
  These examples are not exhaustive nor guaranteed to be secure on their own. Each one isolates a
  single issue and its fix for study. Real programs combine multiple checks, and a clean entry here
  does not mean a program built around that pattern is automatically safe.
</Callout>

# verifiable-builds.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/security/verifiable-builds.mdx

title: Verifiable builds
description: Use Anchor's Docker-backed CLI to produce reproducible Solana program binaries that can be verified against a deployed program.

Building Solana programs with the Solana CLI can embed machine-specific code into the resulting binary, so the same source on different machines may produce different executables. Anchor solves this by building inside a Docker image with pinned dependencies, producing a verifiable build.

[Install Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) first, then use the Anchor CLI commands below.

## Building

Produce a verifiable build:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> build <dim>--verifiable</dim>
```

## Verifying

Verify a build against a program deployed on mainnet:

```console
$ <blue>anchor</blue> verify <dim>-p</dim> <dim><lib-name></dim> <dim><program-id></dim>
```

The `<lib-name>` is the library name defined in the program's `Cargo.toml{:file}`. If the program has an IDL, the IDL deployed on chain is also checked against the local IDL.

## Images

A Docker image for each version of Anchor is published on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/solanafoundation/anchor) under tags of the form `solanafoundation/anchor:<dim><version></dim>`. To pull the image for Anchor `v1.0.1`:

```console
$ <blue>docker</blue> pull solanafoundation/anchor:v1.0.1
```

## Removing an image

If a CLI verifiable build exits prematurely, the underlying Docker container may still be running in the background. Remove it with:

```console
$ <blue>docker</blue> rm <dim>-f</dim> anchor-program
```

`anchor-program` is the default image name the Anchor CLI uses.

# litesvm.mdx

Source: https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor/blob/master/docs-v2/src/content/docs/v1/testing/litesvm.mdx

title: LiteSVM
description: Write tests for Solana programs in Rust, TS/JS or Python using LiteSVM.

[`litesvm`](https://github.com/LiteSVM/litesvm) is a fast and lightweight library for testing Solana programs. It works by creating an in-process Solana VM optimized for program developers, making it much faster to run and compile than alternatives like `solana-program-test` and `solana-test-validator`. `litesvm` is available in Rust, TS/JS, and Python (as part of the [`solders`](https://pypi.org/project/solders/) library).

## Installation

<Tabs items={['Rust', 'TS/JS', 'Python']}>
<Tab>

```console showLineNumbers=false
<blue>cargo</blue> add litesvm <dim>--dev</dim>
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```console showLineNumbers=false
<blue>npm</blue> i litesvm <dim>-D</dim>
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```console showLineNumbers=false
<blue>uv</blue> add solders # from solders import litesvm
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Minimal example

<Tabs items={['Rust', 'TypeScript', 'Python']}>
<Tab>

```rust showLineNumbers=false
use litesvm::LiteSVM;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
use solana_system_interface::instruction::transfer;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;

let from_keypair = Keypair::new();
let from = from_keypair.pubkey();
let to = Pubkey::new_unique();

let mut svm = LiteSVM::new();
svm.airdrop(&from, 10_000).unwrap();

let instruction = transfer(&from, &to, 64);
let tx = Transaction::new(
    &[&from_keypair],
    Message::new(&[instruction], Some(&from)),
    svm.latest_blockhash(),
);
let tx_res = svm.send_transaction(tx).unwrap();

let from_account = svm.get_account(&from);
let to_account = svm.get_account(&to);
assert_eq!(from_account.unwrap().lamports, 4936);
assert_eq!(to_account.unwrap().lamports, 64);
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```ts showLineNumbers=false
import { LiteSVM } from 'litesvm'
import { PublicKey, Transaction, SystemProgram, Keypair, LAMPORTS_PER_SOL } from '@solana/web3.js'

test('one transfer', () => {
  const svm = new LiteSVM()
  const payer = new Keypair()
  svm.airdrop(payer.publicKey, BigInt(LAMPORTS_PER_SOL))
  const receiver = PublicKey.unique()
  const blockhash = svm.latestBlockhash()
  const transferLamports = 1_000_000n
  const ixs = [
    SystemProgram.transfer({
      fromPubkey: payer.publicKey,
      toPubkey: receiver,
      lamports: transferLamports,
    }),
  ]
  const tx = new Transaction()
  tx.recentBlockhash = blockhash
  tx.add(...ixs)
  tx.sign(payer)
  svm.sendTransaction(tx)
  const balanceAfter = svm.getBalance(receiver)
  expect(balanceAfter).toBe(transferLamports)
})
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```python showLineNumbers=false
from solders.keypair import Keypair
from solders.litesvm import LiteSVM
from solders.message import Message
from solders.pubkey import Pubkey
from solders.system_program import transfer
from solders.transaction import VersionedTransaction

def test_transfer() -> None:
    receiver = Pubkey.new_unique()
    client = LiteSVM()
    payer = Keypair()
    client.airdrop(payer.pubkey(), 1_000_000_000)
    blockhash = client.latest_blockhash()
    transfer_lamports = 1_000_000
    ixs = [
        transfer(
            {
                "from_pubkey": payer.pubkey(),
                "to_pubkey": receiver,
                "lamports": transfer_lamports,
            }
        )
    ]
    msg = Message.new_with_blockhash(ixs, payer.pubkey(), blockhash)
    tx = VersionedTransaction(msg, [payer])
    client.send_transaction(tx)
    balance_after = client.get_balance(receiver)
    assert balance_after == transfer_lamports
```

</Tab>

## Deploying programs

Testing real programs goes beyond simple token transfers. Add a compiled program to a test with [`.add_program_from_file(){:rs}`](https://docs.rs/litesvm/latest/litesvm/struct.LiteSVM.html#method.add_program_from_file).

<Callout variant="tip" title="Pulling a program from a cluster">
  To pull a Solana program from mainnet or devnet, use the `$ <blue>solana</blue> program dump`
  command from the Solana CLI.
</Callout>

The following example uses a [simple logging program](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana-program-library/tree/bd216c8103cd8eb9f5f32e742973e7afb52f3b81/examples/rust/logging) from the Solana Program Library:

<Tabs items={['Rust', 'TypeScript', 'Python']}>
<Tab>

```rust showLineNumbers=false
use {
    litesvm::LiteSVM,
    solana_instruction::{account_meta::AccountMeta, Instruction},
    solana_keypair::Keypair,
    solana_pubkey::{pubkey, Pubkey},
    solana_message::{Message, VersionedMessage},
    solana_signer::Signer,
    solana_transaction::VersionedTransaction,
};

fn test_logging() {
    let program_id = pubkey!("Logging111111111111111111111111111111111111");
    let account_meta = AccountMeta {
        pubkey: Pubkey::new_unique(),
        is_signer: false,
        is_writable: true,
    };
    let ix = Instruction {
        program_id,
        accounts: vec![account_meta],
        data: vec![5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14],
    };
    let mut svm = LiteSVM::new();
    let payer = Keypair::new();
    let bytes = include_bytes!("../../node-litesvm/program_bytes/spl_example_logging.so");
    svm.add_program(program_id, bytes);
    svm.airdrop(&payer.pubkey(), 1_000_000_000).unwrap();
    let blockhash = svm.latest_blockhash();
    let msg = Message::new_with_blockhash(&[ix], Some(&payer.pubkey()), &blockhash);
    let tx = VersionedTransaction::try_new(VersionedMessage::Legacy(msg), &[payer]).unwrap();
    // simulate first
    let sim_res = svm.simulate_transaction(tx.clone()).unwrap();
    let meta = svm.send_transaction(tx).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(sim_res.meta, meta);
    assert_eq!(meta.logs[1], "Program log: static string");
    assert!(meta.compute_units_consumed < 10_000) // not being precise here in case it changes
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```ts showLineNumbers=false
import { LiteSVM, TransactionMetadata } from 'litesvm'
import {
  Keypair,
  LAMPORTS_PER_SOL,
  PublicKey,
  Transaction,
  TransactionInstruction,
} from '@solana/web3.js'

test('spl logging', () => {
  const programId = PublicKey.unique()
  const svm = new LiteSVM()
  svm.addProgramFromFile(programId, 'program_bytes/spl_example_logging.so')
  const payer = new Keypair()
  svm.airdrop(payer.publicKey, BigInt(LAMPORTS_PER_SOL))
  const blockhash = svm.latestBlockhash()
  const ixs = [
    new TransactionInstruction({
      programId,
      keys: [{ pubkey: PublicKey.unique(), isSigner: false, isWritable: false }],
    }),
  ]
  const tx = new Transaction()
  tx.recentBlockhash = blockhash
  tx.add(...ixs)
  tx.sign(payer)
  // simulate first
  const simRes = svm.simulateTransaction(tx)
  const sendRes = svm.sendTransaction(tx)
  if (sendRes instanceof TransactionMetadata) {
    expect(simRes.meta().logs()).toEqual(sendRes.logs())
    expect(sendRes.logs()[1]).toBe('Program log: static string')
  } else {
    throw new Error('Unexpected tx failure')
  }
})
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```python showLineNumbers=false
from pathlib import Path

from solders.instruction import AccountMeta, Instruction
from solders.keypair import Keypair
from solders.litesvm import LiteSVM
from solders.message import Message
from solders.pubkey import Pubkey
from solders.transaction import VersionedTransaction
from solders.transaction_metadata import TransactionMetadata

def test_logging() -> None:
    program_id = Pubkey.from_string("Logging111111111111111111111111111111111111")
    ix = Instruction(
        program_id,
        bytes([5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]),
        [AccountMeta(Pubkey.new_unique(), is_signer=False, is_writable=True)],
    )
    client = LiteSVM()
    payer = Keypair()
    client.add_program_from_file(
        program_id, Path("tests/fixtures/spl_example_logging.so")
    )
    client.airdrop(payer.pubkey(), 1_000_000_000)
    blockhash = client.latest_blockhash()
    msg = Message.new_with_blockhash([ix], payer.pubkey(), blockhash)
    tx = VersionedTransaction(msg, [payer])
    # simulate first
    sim_res = client.simulate_transaction(tx)
    meta = client.send_transaction(tx)
    assert isinstance(meta, TransactionMetadata)
    assert sim_res.meta() == meta
    assert meta.logs()[1] == "Program log: static string"
    assert (
        meta.compute_units_consumed() < 10_000
    )  # not being precise here in case it changes
```
